drinks.title: A Cask of Palo Cortado
drinks.author: Mirko Sacco
steps: STIR González Byass Palo Cortado, Aperitivo Select, Boudier Kaffir lime leaf liqueur, and Nardini Tagiatella with ice and strain into chilled glass.
Garnish with bergamot and rose aroma dry ice.

drinks.title: A Cold Siberian Mule
drinks.author: Federico Balzarini and Giacomo Franceschi
steps: Shake Mamont Vodka, beetroot and green apple syrup, lime juice, Green Chartreuse, egg white and absinthe with ice and strain into a glass filled with ice.

drinks.title: ABC Shot
drinks.history: Amaretto, Baileys and cognac — the initials are the recipe, which is the whole joke and the reason it is easy to order in any language.
steps: Slowly layer amaretto, irish cream and cognac into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Absinthe Drip Cocktail (French method)
drinks.author: Dick Bradsell
steps: Place absinthe in an absinthe glass. Balance an absinthe spoon across the rim of the glass and place a sugar cube on the spoon. Slowly drip water over the sugar cube onto the absinthe below, allowing it to dissolve and dilute the spirit. Once the sugar is dissolved, stir gently and serve.

drinks.title: Absinthe Shot
drinks.history: Absinthe was banned across most of Europe from 1915 on the belief that its wormwood caused madness — it did not; the real culprits were adulterants and sheer strength. The EU relegalised it in 1988, and Britain, which had never banned it, led the 1990s revival.
steps: Pour absinthe and sugar cube into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Absolut Kelly
drinks.author: Ektoras Binikos
steps: Muddle lime wedges with shiso leaf, gum arabic syrup and mastiha water in the base of a shaker.
Add Absolut vodka, Becherovka, lime juice, yuzu juice, and remaining shiso leaves over ice and shake 10 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled glass rimmed with smoked sea salt. Finish with Bergamot bitters and Hella Citrus Bitters.
Garnish with Meyer lemon zest and activated charcoal powder — for visual effect; dissolves completely without staining teeth

drinks.title: Absolut Revival
drinks.author: Thomas Quy
steps: Stir Absolut Vodka, Gancia Bianco vermouth, lime cordial, and plum bitters with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass.
Garnish with dried apple slices.

drinks.title: Adios Motherfucker
drinks.history: Known as the AMF. The Long Island family again, this time with blue curaçao and lemonade, which makes it electric blue. No creator is recorded, which is probably for the best.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add vodka, gin, white rum, tequila, blue curaçao and lemon juice and stir briefly. Top with lemonade.

drinks.title: Advocaat Liqueur
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Combine egg yolks and caster sugar in a bowl and whisk together until pale and creamy.
Slowly add brandy (or neutral spirit) to the egg and sugar mixture, stirring constantly to combine thoroughly.
Stir in vanilla extract and mix well to incorporate.
Transfer the advocaat to bottles for storage. The liqueur will thicken slightly as it cools and matures.
Store in a cool, dark place. Advocaat will keep for several months and develops better flavour over time as the ingredients meld together.

drinks.title: After Eight
drinks.history: Coffee liqueur, crème de menthe and Irish cream, layered to taste like the mint chocolate — which has been made in Britain since 1962.
steps: Slowly layer coffee liqueur, crème de menthe and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Alabama Slammer
drinks.author: Gary Regan
steps: Pour sloe gin, amaretto, and Southern Comfort into a shaker with ice. Add orange juice freshly squeezed. Shake well and strain into a highball glass filled with ice.

drinks.title: Alexander
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add gin, crème de cacao, cream and egg white to a shaker with ice.
Shake vigorously using the dry shake technique to create a smooth emulsion and frothy head.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve.

drinks.title: Algonquin
drinks.author: Difford's Guide & Dean Callan
steps: Combine rye whiskey, pineapple juice, bianco vermouth, and Peychaud's bitters in a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass. This Manhattan-like cocktail balances ripe pineapple fruitiness with the warmth of rye whiskey.

drinks.title: Alien Brain Hemorrhage
drinks.history: The Brain Hemorrhage with blue curaçao added, which turns the curdled cream a colour no food should be. A Halloween drink that stayed on menus.
steps: Pour peach schnapps into a shot glass.
Add blue curaçao, drop in irish cream so it clouds, then a few drops of grenadine.

drinks.title: Almond Martini
steps: Add vodka and amaretto liqueur to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Stir well and strain into a chilled martini glass.
Serve immediately — choose a quality amaretto liqueur made from almonds for the best flavor.

drinks.title: Alpine Negroni
steps: Pour gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth into a mixing glass with ice. Stir well for 30 seconds until chilled and diluted. Strain into a rocks glass filled with ice. Garnish with an orange twist or cherry.

drinks.title: Americano
drinks.history: It began as the Milano-Torino, after the home cities of its two ingredients — Campari from Milan, vermouth from Turin. American tourists took to it so thoroughly that the name changed. It is the first drink James Bond orders in the novels.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add equal parts campari and sweet vermouth.
Top with a splash of soda water and garnish with an orange slice.
-- The Negroni's simpler, gin-free predecessor.

drinks.title: Ameritino
drinks.author: Manolis Lykiardopolous
steps: STIR Martini Rubino, Martini Bitter, espresso coffee and Skinos mastiha with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Top with Three Cents tonic water and garnish with lemon zest twist and fresh marjoram.

drinks.title: Añejo Highball
drinks.history: Dale DeGroff's, from the years at the Rainbow Room that started the American cocktail revival. Aged rum with curaçao, lime and ginger beer.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add aged rum, dry curaçao, lime juice and angostura bitters and stir briefly. Top with ginger beer.

drinks.title: Angel's Kiss
drinks.history: In print by the 1930s, which makes it one of the oldest layered shots still served. Crème de cacao with a float of cream, sometimes with a cherry balanced on a pick across the rim.
steps: Slowly layer crème de cacao and cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Anti Figmatic
drinks.author: Ali Reynolds

ingredients.name: ant infused fig leaf syrup with coconut

steps: Add a pinch of citric acid into a mixing glass and dissolve with Ketel One Vodka, ant infused fig leaf syrup with coconut and Cacao Blanc. Stir over cubed ice and strain into a cocktail glass.

drinks.title: Aperol Spritz
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour Soave wine into a glass filled with ice.
Add Aperol Aperitivo.
Top with soda water.
Stir gently to combine.

drinks.title: Apple Grass
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add bison grass vodka, spiced vanilla liqueur, ginger syrup, apple juice, and lemon juice to a shaker filled with ice. Shake well and strain into a chilled glass.
A brilliant "grassy" cocktail for the only Grand Slam tournament played on grass.

drinks.title: Apple Pie Shot
drinks.history: Vodka and apple juice with cinnamon. One of the dessert shots that followed the sweet-schnapps boom; no origin is recorded.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka and apple schnapps briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass. Garnish with a dusting of cinnamon.

drinks.title: Appletini
drinks.history: Credited to Adam Karsten at Lola's. It became the emblem of the 1990s wave of sweet drinks that qualified as martinis purely by being served in the glass.
steps: Shake vodka, apple schnapps and apple juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with a slice of apple.
-- A 1990s bar-menu favourite — not a true martini, just borrows the glass.

drinks.title: Appletini (Sour Apple Martini)
drinks.author: Difford's Guide
steps: Add vodka, sour apple liqueur, sugar syrup, lime cordial, lime juice and lemon juice to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled martini glass.

drinks.title: Aristocracy
drinks.author: N. Bakoulis and V. Kyritsis
steps: For the Mediterranean elixir, heat flat Aegean tonic, sugar, star anise, cardamom, clarified tomato water, citric acid, and celery bitters together using a sous vide 2 hours at 50°C. Strain and refrigerate until ready to use.
Pour cherry Heering and old Tom gin into an ice-filled glass. Top with Mediterranean elixir dispensed from a cream syphon. Stir briefly and garnish with a mint sprig.

drinks.title: Arnold Palmer
steps: Brew breakfast tea and let cool. Pour iced tea into a glass with ice. Add freshly made lemonade and stir gently to combine. Serve immediately while chilled.

drinks.title: Audaz Cocktail
drinks.author: Adrián Madio
steps: Prepare the Colombian Coffee Balsamic ahead of time: place balsamic vinegar and ground Colombian coffee in a bowl and let infuse 23 hours. Filter through a cloth colander, then add simple syrup (made from equal parts sugar and water).
Prepare the garnish by stuffing cherry with Colombian coffee beans grains, coat with chocolate, top with Maldon salt flakes pinch, and chill until ready to serve.
In a mixing glass, combine Bulleit Rye, Cherry Heering, Oloroso Sherry, and Colombian Coffee Balsamic. Add ice cubes and stir to chill and dilute 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass over translucent ice cube large. Garnish with the stuffed cherry and a yellow flower. Finish with a spritz of Coffee Heering fragrance.

drinks.title: Autumn Colour
drinks.author: Jienming Liao

ingredients.name: Pagoda Chinese Yellow Wine Semi Dry

steps: Add Cointreau, Pagoda Chinese Yellow Wine Semi Dry, Osmanthus Verjus, and Sotol La Higuera to a cocktail shaker with ice and shake well.
Strain into a Margarita glass rimmed with dried plum powder. Spray with Sotol over the top.

drinks.title: Autumn Leaves
drinks.author: Myles Davies
steps: Stir Jameson Irish Whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Kingston Black Apple Aperitif over ice in a mixing glass for 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and add liquorice bitters.

drinks.title: Aviation Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford (adapted from Hugo R. Ensslin)
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, maraschino liqueur, and crème de violette well in a mixing glass with cracked ice 10 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve straight-up.

drinks.title: B-52
drinks.history: Peter Fich, head bartender at the Banff Springs Hotel, named his layered shots after bands he liked, and this one after the B-52s. The layers hold because each liqueur is less dense than the one below it.
steps: Layer coffee liqueur, then irish cream, then orange liqueur carefully over the back of a spoon in a shot glass so each stays separate.
-- The layering trick works because each liqueur is a slightly different density — pour slowly.

drinks.title: B-53
drinks.history: A B-52 with sambuca swapped in. The B-51, B-54 and B-55 all follow the same joke, and none of them has a recorded creator.
steps: Slowly layer coffee liqueur, irish cream and sambuca into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Baby Guinness
drinks.history: Coffee liqueur with a float of Irish cream, so that it looks like a miniature pint of stout. There is no Guinness in it at all.
steps: Slowly layer coffee liqueur and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Bacardi Cocktail
drinks.place: Havana, Cuba, then New York, USA
drinks.history: A daiquiri built specifically on Bacardi rum, and the centre of a 1936 New York court case: the Bacardi company sued two bars for serving the drink with a different rum, and won. Since then, by definition, only Bacardi rum makes a true Bacardi Cocktail.
steps: Shake white rum, lime juice, sugar syrup and grenadine hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A 1930s New York court case ruled this drink legally must be made with Bacardi rum specifically to bear the name.

drinks.title: Bad Blood
drinks.author: Evelyn Chick
steps: Pour Laphroaig Select, LBV port, Cherry Heering, and Spanish sweet vermouth over one large ice cube in an old-fashioned glass. Stir to dilute 30 seconds. Garnish with an orange zest twist.

drinks.title: Bahama Mama
drinks.history: A tourist-trade drink built to use the islands' rum. It is often credited to the bartender Oswald Greenslade, though the documentary record is thin.
steps: Shake dark rum, coconut rum, orange juice, pineapple juice and grenadine hard with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass over ice and garnish with a pineapple wedge.
-- A Caribbean resort-bar staple, built for poolside drinking rather than precision.

drinks.title: Banana Daiquiri
drinks.history: El Floridita acquired an electric blender and Constantino Ribalaigua began serving the daiquiri as snow. Every frozen cocktail on every beach descends from it.
steps: Blend white rum, banana, lime juice and sugar syrup with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass.
-- A frozen twist on the classic Daiquiri, built around a whole banana rather than shaken with ice.

drinks.title: Bandera
steps: Pour lime juice into a shot glass to represent the green of the Mexican flag.
Follow with Blanco tequila to represent the white of the Mexican flag.
Chase with Sangrita to represent the red of the Mexican flag. — The three ingredients are traditionally drunk in quick succession as separate shots rather than mixed together

drinks.title: Batida Rosa
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour cachaça, pineapple juice, lemon juice and grenadine syrup into a glass filled with ice. Top with soda water and stir well.

drinks.title: Battle of Carabobo Cocktail
drinks.author: Ezra Star
steps: Stir Santa Theresa 1794 rum, Palo Cortado sherry, Cherry Heering, and Cinzano Sweet vermouth with ice. Strain into an old-fashioned glass over a large cube of ice.
Add Angostura Aromatic Bitters to finish. Garnish with an orange zest twist.

drinks.title: Bay Breeze
drinks.history: A Sea Breeze with pineapple in place of grapefruit, one of a whole family — Cape Codder, Sea Breeze, Bay Breeze, Madras — built on the back of the cranberry juice boom.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add vodka, pineapple juice and cranberry juice.
Stir gently and garnish with a lime wedge.
-- A tropical cousin of the Sea Breeze, with pineapple juice swapped in for grapefruit.

drinks.title: Bazooka Joe
drinks.history: Banana liqueur, blue curaçao and Irish cream, named after the bubblegum and its comic-strip mascot.
steps: Slowly layer blue curaçao, banana liqueur and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Bee's Knees
drinks.history: Honey and lemon do a great deal to disguise rough gin, which is exactly what was available in 1920s America. The name was slang of the day for something excellent. It is often credited to Frank Meier at the Ritz in Paris.
steps: Shake gin, honey syrup and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A Prohibition-era invention where honey helped mask the taste of rough, home-distilled gin.

drinks.title: Bellini
drinks.history: Giuseppe Cipriani at Harry's Bar named it after the pink light in a painting by Giovanni Bellini. It must be white peach purée and prosecco — Cipriani made it only when white peaches were in season.
steps: Add peach purée to a chilled champagne flute.
Top slowly with prosecco and stir gently to combine.
-- Invented at Harry's Bar in Venice in the 1930s, named for its pink hue reminding the creator of a saint's robe in a Bellini painting.

drinks.title: Berlusconi's Love Child
steps: Pour equal parts Monkey Shoulder, Amaro and Crème de Pèche into a mixing glass with ice. Stir well 20 seconds until chilled and properly diluted. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: Between the Sheets
drinks.history: From Harry MacElhone's Harry's New York Bar — a Sidecar with rum added to the brandy. The name means exactly what it appears to.
steps: Shake white rum, cognac, triple sec and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A Prohibition-era favourite, similar in structure to a Sidecar with rum added.

drinks.title: Bicicletta Spritz
steps: Pour Pinot Grigio into a wine glass filled with ice. Top with Prosecco and Campari. Stir gently to combine and garnish with an orange slice or twist.

drinks.title: Bijou
drinks.history: Credited to Harry Johnson, whose Bartenders' Manual presents the three ingredients as jewels — gin for diamond, vermouth for ruby, green Chartreuse for emerald. Bijou is French for jewel.
steps: Stir gin, sweet vermouth and green chartreuse with ice and a dash of orange bitters.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a cherry.
-- French for "jewel" — gin, vermouth and chartreuse are meant to represent diamond, ruby and emerald.

drinks.title: BJØRK / BIRCH
drinks.author: Carl Wiman
steps: Prepare the birch-infused Martini Bianco by infusing dried birch leaves into Martini Bianco for 30 minutes. Strain and keep cool.
Pour HIMKOK Old Tom Gin and birch-infused Martini Bianco into a stirring glass, add ice and stir down to proper dilution depending on your ice quality.
Spray the glass with Lagavulin 16.
Strain the cocktail into the glass and garnish with Kraftkar blue cheese stuffed olive.

drinks.title: Black Russian
drinks.history: Gustave Tops made it at the Hotel Metropole for Perle Mesta, the US ambassador to Luxembourg. The Russian in the name is the vodka and nothing else; the drink is Belgian.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Add vodka and coffee liqueur, then stir gently.
-- Created in 1949 by a Belgian barman for the US ambassador to Luxembourg — the White Russian is this drink with cream floated on top.

drinks.title: Black Tuxedo
drinks.author: Giovanni Graziadei
steps: Stir Hankey Bannister Original, Martini Rosso vermouth, Fino sherry, Crème de poire liqueur, and Absinthe with ice and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a lemon zest twist.

drinks.title: Black Velvet
drinks.history: Made at Brooks's Club in the week Prince Albert died, on the reasoning that even the champagne should be in mourning — so it was blacked out with stout.
steps: Pour chilled stout slowly into a chilled flute, then top gently with chilled champagne.
-- Created in London to mourn Prince Albert's death in 1861, pairing dark stout with pale champagne.

drinks.title: Blood and Sand
drinks.history: Named after the Rudolph Valentino bullfighting film of that year, and printed in The Savoy Cocktail Book in 1930. Scotch with orange juice sounds wrong and works.
steps: Shake blended scotch, sweet vermouth, cherry liqueur and orange juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Named after the 1922 Rudolph Valentino bullfighting film — one of the few classics built on scotch and orange juice together.

drinks.title: Bloody Mary (Fernand Petiot's Original Recipe)
drinks.author: Fernand Petiot
steps: Cover the bottom of a shaker with salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper and a layer of Worcestershire sauce.
Add lemon juice and ice (cracked).
Add vodka and tomato juice (thick tomato juice preferred).
Shake well and strain into a glass filled with ice.
Pour and serve.

drinks.title: Blow Job
drinks.history: Topped with whipped cream and traditionally drunk with hands behind the back, which is the entire reason for the name and the drink.
steps: Slowly layer coffee liqueur and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands. Garnish with a swirl of whipped cream on top.

drinks.title: Blue Hawaii
drinks.history: Harry Yee created it at the Hilton Hawaiian Village when a blue curaçao sales representative asked him to find a use for it. Yee is also the man who put the paper parasol in tiki drinks.
steps: Blend white rum, blue curaçao, pineapple juice, cream of coconut and lemon juice with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth, then pour into a Hurricane glass.

drinks.title: Blue Hawaiian
drinks.history: Harry Yee created it at the Hilton Hawaiian Village when a blue curaçao sales representative asked him to find a use for it. Yee is also the man who put the paper parasol in tiki drinks.
steps: Blend white rum, blue curaçao, coconut cream and pineapple juice with a handful of ice until smooth.
Pour into a hurricane glass and garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry.
-- Created at a Hawaiian hotel in the 1950s specifically to show off the vivid blue of curaçao.

drinks.title: Blue Kamikaze
drinks.history: A Kamikaze with blue curaçao in place of the triple sec. Both are orange liqueurs, so the change is entirely visual — which was the fashion.
steps: Shake vodka, blue curaçao and lime juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Blue Lagoon
drinks.history: Andy MacElhone made it at Harry's New York Bar, his father's bar, using the blue curaçao then newly fashionable. The colour is the entire idea.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add vodka and blue curaçao, then top with lemonade.
Stir gently and garnish with a slice of lemon.
-- Invented in 1960s Paris — its vivid blue colour comes entirely from the curaçao liqueur.

drinks.title: Bobby Burns (Difford's own)
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour Scotch whisky, rosso vermouth, absinthe and a dash of Peychaud's Bitters into a mixing glass with ice.
Stir well 30 seconds and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a lemon twist or cherry.

drinks.title: Bobby Burns Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add scotch whisky, sweet vermouth, Peychaud's bitters, and absinthe to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Squeeze a lemon peel over the drink and serve.

drinks.title: Boulevardier
drinks.history: Harry MacElhone printed it in Barflies and Cocktails and credited it to Erskine Gwynne, a wealthy American who edited a Paris magazine called The Boulevardier. It is a Negroni with bourbon in place of the gin, and rather better for it in winter.
steps: Stir bourbon, sweet vermouth and campari with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice and garnish with an orange twist.
-- Essentially a Negroni with whiskey standing in for the gin.

drinks.title: Brain Hemorrhage
drinks.history: Peach schnapps with Irish cream dropped in, which the acidity curdles into strands, and a trail of grenadine. The curdling is the point, not a mistake.
steps: Pour peach schnapps into a shot glass.
Slowly add irish cream so it curdles, then drizzle grenadine through it.

drinks.title: Bramble
drinks.history: Dick Bradsell made it at Fred's Club in Soho, wanting something recognisably English. He said he had blackberry picking on the beach at Hastings in mind. It is one of the few British cocktails of the era to become a global standard.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice, then drizzle blackberry liqueur over the top so it bleeds through.
Garnish with a blackberry.
-- Created by Dick Bradsell in 1980s London; the crème de mûre "bleed" is the whole point.

drinks.title: Bramble Cocktail
drinks.author: Dick Bradsell
steps: Fill an old-fashioned glass with crushed ice.
Add gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup. Stir well.
Top up with more crushed ice.
Slowly pour crème de mûre over the fresh ice to create a pleasing bleeding effect in the glass.
Garnish with blackberry and lemon slice. Serve immediately with short straws.

drinks.title: Brandy Alexander
steps: Add brandy, crème de cacao, and heavy cream to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Serve immediately.

drinks.title: Brandy Sour
drinks.history: A colonial-era import that never left: British officers stationed in Cyprus took to it, and it became the island's de facto national drink, still served everywhere from tavernas to five-star hotels.
steps: Shake cognac, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice and garnish with a cherry and orange slice.
-- Cyprus's unofficial national drink, where it's typically made much sweeter than elsewhere.

drinks.title: Brave Bull
drinks.history: A Black Russian with tequila in place of the vodka. Two ingredients, one of the shortest recipes in the book.
steps: Fill a Rocks glass with ice, add tequila and coffee liqueur and stir briefly.

drinks.title: Brazuca Remedy
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add basil leaves to a shaker and gently muddle to release oils. Add silver cachaça, limoncello, orange-red aperitivo, lemon juice, honey syrup and pasteurised egg white to the shaker with ice and shake vigorously 10 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass. — Bittersweet and complex with underlying cachaça character. Perfect as an aperitivo.

drinks.title: Breakfast at Julio's
steps: Add ginger ground dried, cardamom ground, and English Breakfast Tea to a teapot, add water and infuse 4 minutes, stirring twice while brewing.
Fine-strain the tea into a pre-heated glass, add agave syrup and stir with cinnamon stick.
Add tequila reposado, stir again and leave the cinnamon stick to infuse in the drink 2 minutes prior to serving.
Garnish with orange zest (discarded).

drinks.title: Breakfast in Bed
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "bright, fragrant, zesty" — lemon-infused gin lengthened with a black tea syrup, in the mould of a gin fizz. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake lemon-infused Boatyard gin, black tea syrup and lemon juice hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass or over fresh ice in a rocks glass. Garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Bright, fragrant and zesty, per the bar's own menu — a good one for someone who wants a G&T with a bit more going on.

drinks.title: Breakfast in Blenheim
drinks.author: Marcus Heale

ingredients.name: tomato soup and pureed baked bean juice blend
English Breakfast Bloody Mary spice mix

steps: Stir Chase Smoked Vodka, tomato soup and pureed baked bean juice blend, and English Breakfast Bloody Mary spice mix briefly to loosen up the ingredients.
Add cubed ice and stir gently to chill.
Strain over fresh cubed ice into a Collins glass rimmed with Tyrrells salt and black pepper, crushed and cracked together.
Garnish with streaky bacon, scotch quail egg, and top with Williams Chase Apple Gin sauce (a reduction made from gin, cooking apples, sugar, and water).
Serve on a copper tray accompanied by eggs, bacon, and sausage.

drinks.title: Breakfast Martini
steps: Combine gin, marmalade, and fresh orange juice in a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled Martini glass.
Serve immediately as an eminently palatable breakfast cocktail.

drinks.title: Brewing the Perfect Cup of Tea
drinks.author: Robert Schinkel
steps: Select spring water with a neutral pH value, low in calcium and magnesium, and with a TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) number between 30 and 150 parts per million. Micro-filtered water or water from reverse osmosis will also work well.
Boil the water only once, as re-boiling reduces CO2 levels and decreases acidity, which affects the complexity and character of your brew.
Allow the boiled water to cool for approximately 2 minutes, as it loses roughly 10°C of temperature per minute after boiling.
Use roughly tea for water. Pour the water over the tea leaves and stir a few times. Agitating the leaves while brewing helps the full character of the tea to develop.

Brew for the appropriate time based on your tea type — white teas typically 3-5 minutes, green teas 3-5 minutes, oolong teas 5-8 minutes, and black teas 4-5 minutes. Refer to the brewing chart for your specific tea variety to avoid over-brewing, which results in bitterness, or under-brewing, which results in weak, characterless tea.

Serve most teas plain to preserve their character. White, green and oolong teas are best enjoyed without additions. Full-bodied black teas can be served the traditional British way with milk and optionally sugar for balance. For cocktails or punches, brew a strong cup so the tea flavor is not lost when combined with ice, spirits, sweeteners, bitters or juices.

drinks.title: Bronx Cocktail
drinks.history: Named for the Bronx Zoo, and said to have been created by Johnnie Solon at the Waldorf-Astoria after a customer described a drink he'd had that reminded him of the zoo's monkey house. Gin, orange juice and both vermouths — briefly one of New York's most popular cocktails before falling out of fashion.
steps: Shake gin, dry vermouth, sweet vermouth and orange juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A once-ubiquitous early-1900s classic, effectively a Martini crossed with a Manhattan.

drinks.title: Brooklyn
drinks.history: First appeared in print in 1908 and is credited to bartender Jack Grohusko, in a version with sweet vermouth. The now-standard dry vermouth version comes from the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.
steps: Stir rye whiskey, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur and Amer Picon with ice until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a cherry.
notes: Standard 2 oz / 1 oz / 1/4 oz / 1/4 oz build. Amer Picon is hard to find outside Europe; Ramazzotti, Bigallet China-China or CioCiaro are common substitutes. Some sites list smaller vermouth amounts.

drinks.title: Brooklyn Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add rye whisky, sweet vermouth, Amer Picon, and maraschino liqueur to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 30 seconds until chilled and diluted.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve up without garnish, or with a cherry if preferred.

drinks.title: Brown Chicken, Brown Cacao
drinks.author: Kate Gerwin
steps: In an ISI container, rapidly infuse Bols Cacao Brown, Bols Natural Yoghurt and spiced almond milk with cardamom seeds, cinnamon stick, and star anise pods. Then strain the infusion and combine with Bols Cacao White and black walnut bitters in a perlini shaker.
Add ice, shake, carbonate and strain into the milk jug glass.
Top with Bols Cacao White foam and grated nutmeg. Serve with a candy striped straw.

drinks.title: Brown Derby
drinks.history: Named after the Brown Derby restaurant, though it was probably created at the Vendôme Club nearby. Bourbon, grapefruit and honey — a Prohibition-repeal drink that reads as thoroughly modern.
steps: Shake bourbon, grapefruit juice and honey syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Named for the famous Hollywood restaurant shaped like a hat, a Prohibition-era favourite of the film crowd.

drinks.title: Brownie Cocktail
steps: This rich and chocolatey cocktail celebrates National Brownie Day. Combine crème de cacao, chocolate liqueur, and vodka in a cocktail shaker with ice. Shake well 10 seconds and strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Top with a splash of cream for a decadent finish.

drinks.title: Bubblegum Shot
drinks.history: Banana and strawberry liqueurs with cream, which together land on the flavour of the sweet. One of the many shooters of the decade with no recorded creator.
steps: Shake vodka, banana liqueur, blue curaçao and cream briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Buck's Fizz
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour champagne into a coupe glass, then top with orange juice made from freshly squeezed oranges chilled straight from the refrigerator. Stir gently and serve immediately without ice.

drinks.title: Buttery Nipple
drinks.history: Butterscotch schnapps with a cream float, from the same wave of layered shooters. Butterscotch schnapps barely existed before the 1980s and defined the decade's bar once it did.
steps: Slowly layer butterscotch schnapps and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Cable Car
drinks.history: Created by Tony Abou-Ganim in 1996 at the Starlight Room in San Francisco, after Captain Morgan asked him to develop a drink around their spiced rum. It is built on the Sidecar template with spiced rum in place of brandy.
steps: Rim a chilled coupe glass with cinnamon sugar. Shake spiced rum, orange curaçao, lemon juice and simple syrup hard with ice.
Strain into the prepared glass and garnish with an orange twist.
notes: Follows Punch's 1 1/2 oz / 3/4 oz / 1 oz / 1/2 oz spec, matched by Elevated Craft. Dan Murphy's gives a slightly lighter metric version (40/20/25/15 ml).

drinks.title: Cactus Jack
drinks.history: Tequila with melon liqueur and citrus. Named for the cactus, though agave is not one — it is closer to asparagus and lilies than to anything spiny in a desert.
steps: Shake tequila, melon liqueur and lime juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Cadillac Margarita
drinks.history: A regular margarita with a float of Grand Marnier in place of the triple sec — the \"top-shelf\" upgrade that gave the drink its name, on the reasoning that a Cadillac was the top-shelf car.
steps: Run a lime wedge around the rim of a chilled glass and dip it in salt to coat.
Shake tequila, grand marnier and lime juice hard with ice, then strain into the glass over fresh ice.
-- A top-shelf Margarita finished with orange-flavoured Grand Marnier instead of plain triple sec.

drinks.title: Caipirinha
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Wash lime and cut off the very ends of its poles (top & tail) before cutting in half from pole to pole.
Take one half of the lime and slice into 3-4 mm thick half-moon shaped segments.
Transfer the chopped lime into a robust shatterproof rocks glass.
Add caster sugar and muddle.
Depending on your ice, consider adding water chilled, or alternatively add fruit (or strawberries or kiwi) and muddle some more.
When muddling has fully extracted the juice from the fruit and the sugar is dissolved, tip the muddled fruit and sugar into a serving highball glass.
Pour cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass and swirl to rinse before pouring into the serving glass. Stir to ensure cachaça is well mixed with fruit.
Crack four large ice cubes and drop them into the serving glass.
Stir before adding more ice and then serve with a stirrer but no straws.

drinks.title: Campari Spritz
drinks.history: The older and more bitter sibling of the Aperol Spritz, from the same Austrian habit of spraying water into strong Veneto wine. Campari has been made to Gaspare Campari's 1860 recipe ever since, and its recipe is still secret.
steps: Fill a Wine glass with ice, add campari and stir briefly. Top with prosecco. Garnish with an orange slice.

drinks.title: Candy on the Coast
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "velvety, creamy, sweet" — raspberry-infused vodka and Amarula with strawberry and a candy floss syrup, finished with cream. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake raspberry-infused vodka, Amarula, strawberry syrup, candy floss syrup and cream hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a swirl of candy floss if you have it.
notes: Velvety, creamy and sweet, per the bar's own menu — a genuine dessert cocktail, best treated as one.

drinks.title: Cantarito Cocktail
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: In a small jar or cocktail shaker, combine grapefruit juice, orange juice, lime juice, and simple syrup. Shake or stir well, then set aside.
Run a lime wedge around the outside rim of each cantarito or glass. Dip the rims into a plate of chile powder mix to coat.
Fill each glass with crushed ice, then add tequila blanco to each and stir to chill.
Divide the citrus juice mixture evenly and pour it between the two glasses.
Top each cantarito with grapefruit soda and garnish with grapefruit wedges and orange wedges.

drinks.title: Cantineros Gentleman Daiquiri
drinks.author: Mario Hofferer
steps: Flambé rosemary then place into a shaker. Add Bacardi Superior rum, cherry eau de vie, lemon juice, white caster sugar, and grapefruit juice. Add ice and shake vigorously 10 seconds. Double strain into a pre-chilled or frozen cocktail glass.
Garnish with rose petal and gold sugar pearls.

drinks.title: Cape Codder
drinks.history: Invented by Ocean Spray as the Red Devil to sell cranberry juice, and renamed the Cape Codder in the 1960s when the co-operative pushed it into bars.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add vodka and stir briefly. Top with cranberry juice. Garnish with a lime wedge.

drinks.title: Caribbean Colada
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add white rum, aged rum, pineapple liqueur, coconut syrup, passion fruit syrup and orange juice to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled glass.

drinks.title: Cement Mixer
drinks.history: Irish cream held in the mouth alongside lime juice, which sets it solid. A dare rather than a drink, and one no bartender is proud of.
steps: Pour irish cream into a shot glass.
Add lime juice, hold in the mouth for a few seconds to let it curdle, then swallow.

drinks.title: Chaas Recipe (Spiced Indian Buttermilk)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Add yogurt (plain curd made from whole milk), mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chilli (or black pepper crushed), ginger (peeled and fresh), black salt, regular salt, and roasted cumin powder to a blender.

Blend until smooth, then pour in water and lemon juice (optional, skip if yogurt is sour). Blend until frothy. Taste and adjust salt or spices as needed. Add more water if you prefer a thinner consistency.
Pour into serving glasses. Garnish with chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, and fresh coriander leaves or mint leaves.

-- For a version without a blender: Add all ingredients to a mixing bowl and whisk together with a whisk instead of blending. Use the same ingredient quantities. Whisk until smooth, add water, then whisk again until frothy. The leaves will remain in the drink.

drinks.title: Chai Latte Recipe
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Grind or crush cardamom (deseeded), cinnamon stick, black pepper (optional), and cloves to a coarse powder using a spice grinder, mortar and pestle, or rolling pin.

Pour water into a saucepan and add all the ground spices, sugar, and black tea (or 1-1.5 teaspoons loose leaf tea). Bring to a rolling boil over medium-high heat and simmer for 3-4 minutes until reduced to about 80 ml. Add vanilla extract and turn off heat.
For stronger flavors, cover and let steep for 10 minutes. Strain through a strainer to remove spices. Your chai concentrate is ready. Keep warm to serve immediately or refrigerate for later use.
Pour milk into a saucepan and heat over medium-high heat until you see steam rising from the milk (3-4 minutes). Do not boil—turn off heat as soon as steam appears.

Pour the hot milk into a 500 ml heat-proof mason jar (fill only halfway) and secure the lid tightly. Shake the jar carefully until the milk turns frothy, about 25-35 seconds. Alternatively, use a milk frother to froth for 25-35 seconds until foamy.

Pour 125-180 ml of the prepared chai concentrate into a cup or mug. Top with the steamed milk and finish with the milk froth. Garnish with ground cinnamon if desired. Taste and add more concentrate for stronger flavors if preferred.

drinks.title: Champagne Cocktail
drinks.history: In Jerry Thomas's 1862 guide: a sugar cube soaked in Angostura, dropped into champagne. The bubbles keep climbing off the sugar, which is why it never goes flat while you drink it.
steps: Soak a sugar cube in angostura bitters and drop it into a champagne flute.
Top with chilled champagne and garnish with a lemon twist.
-- One of the oldest cocktails still served today, dating to the mid-1800s.

drinks.title: Champagne pour vous et Tatou
drinks.author: Gareth Evans
steps: Stir ketel one vodka, elderflower liqueur, homemade lemon vermouth, aperol, poire william, and absinthe over ice, then carbonate and decant into champagne bottle.
Zest grapefruit into the glass and serve in the champagne bucket on the red carpet, garnished with flash photography, red carpet, and ticket to film festival.

drinks.title: Champs-Élysées
steps: Add cognac, green chartreuse, lemon juice, sugar syrup, and a dash of aromatic bitters to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a lemon twist — This is essentially a Sidecar made with Green Chartreuse in place of triple sec.

drinks.title: Chartreuse Swizzle
drinks.history: Marcovaldo Dionysos built it around green Chartreuse, which is still made by Carthusian monks to a recipe of 130 herbs that only two of them know at a time. Swizzled over crushed ice with a proper swizzle stick.
steps: Build over crushed ice and swizzle with a bar spoon until frosted.
Fill a Highball glass with ice, add green chartreuse, pineapple juice, lime juice and falernum and stir briefly.

drinks.title: Cherry Bakewell
steps: Pour dry vermouth, amaretto, cognac, and cherry brandy liqueur into a cocktail shaker with ice and stir well. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve.

drinks.title: Chi-Chi
drinks.history: A Piña Colada made with vodka in place of the rum, from an era when tiki bars were adding a vodka option to nearly everything on the menu.
steps: Blend vodka, pineapple juice and coconut cream with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and garnish with a wedge of pineapple.
-- A piña colada in all but name, swapping the rum for vodka.

drinks.title: Chocolate Cake
drinks.history: Vodka and hazelnut liqueur, drunk with a sugared lemon wedge. There is no chocolate in it — the lemon and hazelnut together produce the flavour, which is a genuinely odd piece of taste chemistry.
steps: Serve with a sugar-coated lemon wedge to bite after.
Shake vanilla vodka and hazelnut liqueur briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Chocolate Martini
drinks.history: A product of the dessert-cocktail boom. It is often said to have been created for Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton in the 1950s, but no contemporary source supports it.
steps: Shake vodka, crème de cacao and cream hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass rimmed with cocoa powder.
-- Dessert in a glass, popular from the same era as the appletini.

drinks.title: CÎROC Star Martini
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Shake CÎROC French Vanilla Vodka, passionfruit syrup, rhubarb aperitif, white peach puree, and lemon juice with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
Pour champagne into a shot glass and serve alongside. Garnish by floating half a passionfruit in the martini.

drinks.title: Classic Mexican Margarita Recipe
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: For the natural syrup, mix sugar and water in a small saucepan and place over medium-high heat. Stir until sugar has dissolved and the syrup has formed, about 3 minutes. Cool before using to make the cocktail.
Brush the rim of a cocktail glass with lime juice. Spread out sea salt in a small plate and dip the rim of the glass into it to coat. Set aside in the refrigerator.
Put some crushed ice into a cocktail shaker and add tequila Noble Reposado, triple sec liqueur, lime juice, and natural syrup.
Cover and shake vigorously until a mist forms on the outside of the shaker.
Strain into the prepared cocktail glass and decorate with lime.

drinks.title: Clover Club
drinks.history: Named for a men's club of writers and lawyers that met at the Bellevue-Stratford Hotel from 1882. It disappeared after Prohibition along with the fashion for raw egg white, and came back with the cocktail revival of the 2000s.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, raspberry syrup and egg white hard without ice for 15 seconds, then again with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a raspberry.
-- Named after a gentlemen's club in 1900s Philadelphia.

drinks.title: Corn-on-the-Cob
steps: Pour gin and sweet vermouth into a glass filled with ice. Stir well to chill and dilute slightly.
Garnish with baby corn.

drinks.title: Corny Cockney
steps: Shake gin, Jack Daniel's Tennessee whiskey, juice from tinned sweet corn, and 1883 Popcorn Syrup{22%mL} with ice and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Float popcorn air on top and garnish with a cone of popcorn pegged to the rim.

drinks.title: Corpse Reviver No. 1
drinks.history: The brandy-based member of the Savoy's hangover family, and the heavier one. Craddock's note: to be taken before 11am, or whenever steam and energy are needed.
steps: Stir brandy, apple brandy and sweet vermouth with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- The brandy-based half of the Corpse Reviver family, older and steadier than its more famous sibling, No. 2.

drinks.title: Corpse Reviver No. 2
drinks.history: From Harry Craddock's Savoy Cocktail Book, one of a family of drinks meant as morning-after cures. Craddock added his own warning: four taken in swift succession will unrevive the corpse again.
steps: Rinse a chilled coupe glass with a dash of absinthe and discard the excess.
Shake gin, triple sec, lillet blanc and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into the glass.
-- Part of a family of "hair of the dog" morning cocktails — the classic warning is that four of these will "un-revive" you completely.

drinks.title: Cosmopolitan
drinks.place: Disputed — Provincetown, Miami, San Francisco and New York
drinks.history: Cheryl Cook in South Beach claims a mid-1980s version made with citrus vodka and a splash of cranberry for the colour. Toby Cecchini at the Odeon in New York standardised the modern build in 1988. Madonna drinking one in public, and then Sex and the City, made it the drink of the 1990s.
steps: Shake vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice and lime juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with a lime twist.
-- Went from a niche New York drink to a global icon largely thanks to Sex and the City.

drinks.title: Cosmopolitan Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice, lime juice, and a dash of orange bitters to a shaker with ice. Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: Cough Drop
drinks.history: Blackberry brandy and peppermint schnapps, which taste deliberately and unmistakably medicinal. The name is a warning, not a complaint.
steps: Pour jägermeister and blackberry liqueur into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Cuba Libre
drinks.history: After the Spanish-American War, American troops in Havana found Coca-Cola newly available alongside local rum, and toasted the result \"¡Por Cuba libre!\" — to a free Cuba. The lime is not optional.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add white rum and a squeeze of lime juice, then top with cola.
Stir briefly and garnish with a wedge of lime.
-- Cuba's answer to rum and coke — legend has it the name comes from a toast, "¡Por Cuba libre!", during the Spanish–American War.

drinks.title: Cubanisima
drinks.author: Robert Woods
steps: Shake Bacardi Superior rum, Ferrand dry orange curaçao, Martini Rosso vermouth, lemon juice, lime juice, mandarin juice, pomegranate grenadine syrup, and pineapple sherbet with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
Garnish with a small black cherry.

drinks.title: Cubanito Rum Punch (Slushie)
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Add guava juice, pineapple juice, Havana Club 3yo, lime juice, homemade falernum syrup, and fresh raspberries to a slushie machine. Mix well to combine and allow to chill and freeze 120 minutes until the mixture reaches the proper slushie consistency and temperature. Serve in a cup with a paper straw. — This recipe fills one tank; adjust proportions as needed for smaller batches

drinks.title: Culloden Heather
drinks.author: Tomasz Oleksy
steps: Shake Drambuie, Dalmore 12-year-old, pomegranate juice, lemon juice and homemade syrup (cranberry, Campari reduction, strawberry and Angostura Aromatic Bitters) over ice and strain into glass.
Garnish with orange twist. Serve alongside dried oranges and redcurrants dusted with sugar.

drinks.title: Daiquiri
drinks.history: Named after an iron-mining village on Cuba's south coast, where the American engineer Jennings Cox is credited with mixing the rum ration with lime and sugar. Admiral Lucius Johnson carried it to the Army and Navy Club in Washington around 1909, which is how it reached the American mainstream.
steps: Shake white rum, lime juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Ernest Hemingway's favourite bar order, minus the sugar — ask for a "Papa Doble" for his version.

drinks.title: Daiquiri No. 3
drinks.author: Constantino Ribailagua Vert
steps: Add white rum, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a lime wheel or twist.

drinks.title: Dale DeGroff's Rye & Cherry Punch
drinks.author: Dale DeGroff
steps: Make the double shrub first. Using a peeler remove only the zest (no pith) from lemons and oranges. Pound the zests with sugar in a quart container. Screw down the top when finished and shake well right side and upside down. Set aside for 360 minutes.
After 6 hours, add lemon juice, screw down the top and shake well until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Strain the shrub off the lemon and orange zests. The zests can be discarded.

Assemble rye whiskey, Rainwater Madeira, Cherry Heering and the double shrub in a 2 litre batching container. Refill the two whiskey bottles with spring water and add to punch, stir. Keep cold in the fridge until ready to use.

Pour punch into a glass and dust with nutmeg grated. — Recommended rye whiskeys: Rittenhouse Bonded (budget option), E.H. Taylor Bonded Rye (premium option), or Old Forester 1897 if bourbon is preferred

drinks.title: Dark 'n' Stormy
drinks.history: Gosling's Black Seal rum floated on Bermudian ginger beer, said to be named by a sailor who reckoned the colour was that of a cloud only a fool would sail under. Gosling's holds a US trademark on the name, so a bar using any other rum has to call it something else.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add dark rum.
Top with ginger beer and garnish with a lime wedge.
-- Bermuda's national drink, traditionally made with Gosling's Black Seal rum.

drinks.title: Death in the Afternoon
drinks.place: Written for a book, drunk in Paris and Havana
drinks.history: Ernest Hemingway contributed it to a celebrity recipe collection and named it after his bullfighting book. His instruction, printed verbatim: drink three to five of these slowly.
steps: Pour absinthe into a chilled champagne flute and top slowly with champagne.
-- Ernest Hemingway's own recipe, with an instruction to drink "three to five of these slowly."

drinks.title: Dirty Martini
drinks.history: Olive brine stirred into a Martini, first written up in 1901 recipe books under the name \"Dirty Martini\". Franklin D. Roosevelt was known to favour a very dirty one, splashing in a generous measure of the brine.
steps: Stir gin, dry vermouth and olive brine with plenty of ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with olive.
-- A Dry Martini with a splash of olive brine for a savoury edge, "dirtier" the more brine you add.

drinks.title: DIY Rice Milk
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Lightly toast rice grains in a dry frying pan until they start to colour, which should take approximately 5 minutes.
Place the toasted rice into a jar or bowl and soak in water overnight or for about 12 hours.

Once completely soaked, pour both the water and rice grains into a blender, along with salt and your choice of sweetener — honey, sugar, agave syrup or vanilla extract to taste (experiment to see how much you prefer). Blend at the highest speed until completely combined, which should take between 2 minutes and 3 minutes.
Using a cheesecloth or nut milk bag, strain the liquid into a clean bottle and chill before serving. The mixture will need to be shaken before each use.

drinks.title: Dons of Soul
drinks.author: Koji Esashi
steps: Shake Jose Cuervo Especial, fresh lime juice, agave nectar, fresh tomato, red paprika, yellow paprika, hot chilli, and a drop of coriander bitter over ice with 3 twists of pink pepper. Strain into a chilled Martini Chiller Glass.
Garnish with fresh thyme, fresh mint, fresh coriander, a lime peel, and crushed ice mixed with three kinds of Mexican herbs.

drinks.title: Dr Lucy Darawallahs Swamp Fever
drinks.author: Peter
steps: Put the leaves of mint into a pestle and mortar with sugar and bruise it down gently without liquidising. Rinse the pestle and mortar out with a bit of vodka into a large bowl.

Add lime juice (squeezed with pulp) into the bowl along with vodka and white rum and honey (runny). — Start with slightly less honey and add more later if needed. Stir it up so the honey gets mixed in and allow it to marinate in the fridge for 1 day if possible, or 10 minutes if you can't.
Take a large hi ball glass, fill it with whole and half-crushed ice, then half fill with the boozy mixture and top off with ginger beer. — If you don't like ginger beer, try tonic instead.
Drink, share, fall over, and repeat.

drinks.title: Drunk Elephant
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nutty, dense, sweet" — cold brew and cacao playing off the toffee-nut warmth of Amarula and Frangelico, with cacao bitters to round it off. The menu prints the ingredients but not the exact measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate rather than the bar's own recipe card.
steps: Shake Amarula, Frangelico, cold brew coffee, crème de cacao and cacao bitters hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a light grating of cacao or a coffee bean.
notes: Nutty, dense and sweet, closer to a boozy dessert than a bright cocktail — a good one to finish a meal on rather than start with.

drinks.title: Dry Martini
drinks.history: It descends from the Martinez, a much sweeter mix of gin and sweet vermouth, and got progressively drier with every decade of the 20th century until the vermouth was barely a rinse. Recipes under the name appear from the mid-1880s; Harry Johnson printed a recognisable version in 1888.
steps: Stir gin and dry vermouth with plenty of ice for 30 seconds, until very cold.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with olive or a lemon twist.
-- "Dry" refers to the vermouth quantity — less vermouth is drier. Shaken, per Bond, is a matter of taste, not tradition.

drinks.title: Dry Martini 'Preferred' (5:1 ratio)
steps: Stir gin and dry vermouth with ice until well chilled, then strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: Duck Fart
drinks.history: Created at the Peanut Farm bar in Anchorage. It is Alaska's best-known drink, and is layered coffee liqueur, Irish cream and whiskey.
steps: Slowly layer coffee liqueur, irish cream and whisky into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Easter Martini
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Stir vodka, bianco vermouth, white crème de cacao, vanilla liqueur and caramel liqueur with ice in a mixing glass 30 seconds, then strain into a chilled martini glass. Add a dash of chocolate bitters to finish.

drinks.title: Easy Pineapple Margarita
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: Place frozen pineapple chunks, tequila, triple sec, natural sugar syrup, and lime juice in a blender. Blend on the highest setting until you have a very smooth mixture.
Add ice cubes to the blender, making sure they go all the way to the bottom where the blades are, and continue blending until very smooth.
To prepare the glasses, dab the rims with a lime wedge and then dip them into a small plate containing sea salt mixed with piquín powder or cayenne pepper powder if using.
Serve the pineapple margarita in the prepared glasses. Add cherries for garnish and enjoy!

drinks.title: El Diablo
drinks.history: Printed by Trader Vic as the Mexican El Diablo. Tequila with crème de cassis and ginger — a combination almost nobody would think of now, which is why it still surprises.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add tequila, crème de cassis and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir gently.
-- One of the earliest tequila cocktails to appear in an American bar book, dating to the 1940s.

drinks.title: El Presidente
drinks.history: The house drink of Havana's Vedado Tennis Club, named for one Cuban president or another — Mario García Menocal and Gerardo Machado both get the credit. It was the sophisticated end of what Americans drank in Cuba during Prohibition.
steps: Stir white rum, dry vermouth, triple sec and a dash of grenadine with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A stately pre-Prohibition rum cocktail said to be named for a Cuban president.

drinks.title: Elephant 75
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "sweet, tart, dry" — a French 75 built on Copeland Rhuberry gin with a dash of Cointreau added, topped with prosecco. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake Copeland Rhuberry gin, Cointreau, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled Champagne flute. Top with prosecco. Garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Sweet, tart and dry, per the bar's own menu — the rhubarb gin gives it a pink blush and a fruitier edge than a standard French 75.

drinks.title: English Martini
steps: Stir London dry gin, elderflower liqueur, and a splash of dry vermouth with ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with a sprig of fresh rosemary.

drinks.title: Equal Opportunity
drinks.author: Monica Berg
steps: Add aquavit, cherry heering, fino sherry, and pink grapefruit juice to a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake well and fine strain into a chilled old fashioned glass filled with fresh ice.
Garnish with a grapefruit peel twisted over the drink.

drinks.title: Espresso Martini
drinks.history: Dick Bradsell made it at the Soho Brasserie for a model who asked for something that would, in her words, wake her up and then mess her up. He called it a Vodka Espresso first, then the Pharmaceutical Stimulant; the martini name came later and stuck.
steps: Combine vodka, cooled espresso, coffee liqueur, and plenty of ice into a cocktail shaker and rigorously shake until the outside of the shaker is cold. Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with three coffee beans.
notes: A stove-top coffee maker or even canned espresso work just as well if you don't have a coffee machine. Kahlua is the coffee liqueur of choice.

drinks.title: Falernum Liqueur (Historical Recipe)
drinks.author: Mrs. H Graham Yearwood
steps: Combine rum, lime juice, milk, brandy, and sugar in a large vessel. — Based on Mrs. H Graham Yearwood's 1911 recipe scaled from 30 gallons
Add bitter almond and mace to the mixture and stir thoroughly to combine all ingredients.

Allow the mixture to settle and clarify. Add milk to aid in clarification, or use modern filtration equipment to achieve a clear liqueur. — Historical recipe used milk; contemporary methods may substitute fine filtration

Bottle and age the falernum before use in cocktails. The finished liqueur should have a low alcohol content between 11% and 15% alc./vol., with a sweet, syrupy character and subtle spice notes from the cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, ginger and almond flavours.

drinks.title: Far East Julep
drinks.author: Francesco Galdi
steps: Shake Tanqueray Gin, banana liqueur, sugar syrup, fresh lemon juice, lychee juice, fresh passion fruit juice and shiso leaf with ice.
Fine strain into an ice-filled julep cup and top with crushed ice.
Garnish with shiso leaf, half shell of passion fruit with lychee placed inside, and edible flowers.

drinks.title: Fermented Passion Fruit Syrup
drinks.author: Mark Scott
steps: Make a passion fruit syrup by combining caster sugar, soft brown sugar, mineral water (Volvic is recommended) and fresh passion fruits. The syrup should be light and not overly sweet to allow the passion fruit flavour to come through. Use fully ripened, wrinkled fruits for a more pungent, tropical syrup that has begun fermenting naturally.

Once the sugars have dissolved, allow the syrup to cool and infuse for 1 hour. Strain through muslin into a large container, removing large solids without being too aggressive so as not to remove too much flavour. Use a 5 litre jar to ferment 3 litres of syrup, as the container size affects fermentation and expansion.

Prepare the yeast by adding American ale yeast to warm water at 35°C and let it multiply to increase productivity. When the syrup has cooled to 30°C, add the prepared yeast and stir thoroughly to ensure it spreads evenly.

Seal the jar with a pressure-relief valve and leave exposed in a cool cupboard overnight. In the morning, move the jar to a warmer cupboard and leave to ferment for up to 3 days, tasting and smelling daily to monitor development. Agitate the jar occasionally if needed. A foam should settle on top and bubble calmly.

When fermentation is complete to your liking, strain the liquid through muslin again. The finished syrup will be around 2-3% ABV and will last around ten days at optimal freshness. Store in the fridge topped with a rubber wine stopper to keep out unwanted bacteria and prevent CO₂ build-up.

drinks.title: Final Ward
drinks.history: Created by Phil Ward at Death & Co in New York in 2007. It is a riff on the Last Word, swapping the gin for rye and the lime for lemon while keeping the equal-parts structure.
steps: Add rye whiskey, green Chartreuse, maraschino liqueur and lemon juice to a shaker with ice and shake until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Equal parts of 22.5 ml (3/4 oz) as Punch, Difford's and Whisky Advocate agree. Food52 uses a smaller 15 ml build; a bottled-in-bond or 100-proof rye keeps it from tasting thin.

drinks.title: Fireball Shot
drinks.history: Cinnamon whisky created by Seagram in Canada in the 1980s and left to languish. Sazerac relaunched it in 2007 and it became one of the fastest-selling spirits in American history.
steps: Pour cinnamon whisky into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Flatliner
drinks.history: Sambuca, tequila and a line of black pepper across the surface. The pepper sinks through the layers and burns on the way down, which is where the name comes from.
steps: Slowly layer sambuca, tequila and hot sauce into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Floc de Gascogne
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Blend partially fermented grape juice with armagnac to create the base fortified wine. The addition of the spirit raises the alcohol strength to a level which kills the yeast, arresting fermentation and leaving sweet unfermented grape sugars.
Age the fortified wine for at least 9 months in oak casks (optional but traditional).
Serve the Floc de Gascogne chilled or over ice, typically as an aperitif or dessert drink. Consume within one year of release. Once opened, store in a refrigerator and use within three months.

drinks.title: Fluffy Duck
drinks.history: Advocaat and gin lengthened with lemonade. A pub-and-club drink of the era, and still a fixture in Australia.
steps: Shake advocaat, white rum, cointreau, orange juice and cream hard with ice, then strain into a Highball glass over fresh ice. Top with soda water.

drinks.title: Four Horsemen
drinks.history: The Three Wise Men plus José Cuervo, named for the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse. The naming convention tells you everything about the intent.
steps: Pour bourbon, tennessee whiskey, scotch whisky and tequila into a shot glass.

drinks.title: French 1605
steps: This is a tasty riff on a French 75, created to celebrate Chartreuse Day and the 400th anniversary of the Carthusian Monks' Élixir Végétal recipe.
Combine chartreuse verte, gin, and fresh lemon juice in a cocktail shaker with ice cubes. Shake well and strain into a chilled champagne flute.
Top with champagne and stir gently to combine. Garnish with a lemon twist.

drinks.title: French 75
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add lemon juice and powdered sugar to a shaker with dry gin and ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled champagne flute.
Top with champagne and stir gently.
Garnish with a lemon twist.

drinks.title: French Connection
drinks.history: Cognac and amaretto, named after the 1971 film. Part of the same family as the Godfather and Godmother, and just as much a product of amaretto's American marketing.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add cognac and amaretto.
Stir gently.
-- Named after the 1971 film, though the drink itself predates it by some years.

drinks.title: French Martini
drinks.history: It appeared after Chambord reached the American market in 1982. Shaking the pineapple juice hard is what raises the foam on top — there is no egg white in it.
steps: Shake vodka, raspberry liqueur and pineapple juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass.
-- Fruity and pink despite the name — invented in New York, not Paris.

drinks.title: Frozen Daiquiri
drinks.history: El Floridita acquired an electric blender and Constantino Ribalaigua began serving the daiquiri as snow. Every frozen cocktail on every beach descends from it.
steps: Blend white rum, lime juice and sugar syrup with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth, then pour into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Frozen Mango Margarita
drinks.author: Mely Martínez

ingredients.name: chili piquín or cayenne pepper powder

steps: Place mango chunks (frozen), tequila blanco, triple sec, agave syrup, and lime juice in a blender. Blend on the highest setting until you have a very smooth mixture.
Add ice cubes, making sure they go all the way down to the bottom where the blades are, and continue blending until very smooth.

To prepare the glasses, dab the rims with a lime wedge and then dip them into a small plate of salt mixed with chili piquín or cayenne pepper powder (if using). Serve the margarita in the prepared glasses.

drinks.title: Frozen Margarita Recipe
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: Rub the rim of a glass with a lime wedge, then dip the rim into kosher salt spread on a plate.
Combine tequila, triple sec, lime juice, simple syrup, and ice in a blender.
Blend the ingredients until the mixture is smooth and has a slushy consistency.
Pour the frozen margarita mixture into the prepared glass.
Garnish with a lime wedge on the rim or inside the glass.
Serve immediately and enjoy your refreshing frozen margarita!

drinks.title: Fuzzy Navel
drinks.history: Peach schnapps and orange juice, named for the fuzz on a peach's skin and the navel orange in the glass. It arrived with the same peach schnapps boom that gave the decade Sex on the Beach.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add peach schnapps.
Top with orange juice and stir gently.
-- The name is exactly as literal as it sounds — "fuzzy" for the peach, "navel" for the orange.

drinks.title: Gibson
drinks.history: A dry Martini garnished with a cocktail onion instead of an olive. The name is usually credited to the illustrator Charles Dana Gibson, though the story of why is disputed even in the earliest tellings.
steps: Stir gin and dry vermouth with plenty of ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with cocktail onion.
-- A Dry Martini in every way but the garnish — a pickled onion in place of the olive.

drinks.title: Gibson Dry Martini
steps: Stir gin and dry vermouth with ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with cocktail onion.

drinks.title: Gimlet
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Stir gin and Rose's lime cordial with ice and strain into a chilled glass.

drinks.title: Gin & Tonic
steps: Pour gin into a glass filled with ice. Top with tonic water. Stir gently to combine.

drinks.title: Gin and Tonic
drinks.history: Officers of the East India Company took quinine against malaria and found it unbearably bitter, so they cut it with gin, sugar and lime. Commercial tonic water was patented by Erasmus Bond in 1858. Modern tonic has a fraction of the quinine and none of the medical use.
steps: Fill a highball glass with plenty of ice.
Add gin and top with tonic water, stirring gently once.
Garnish with a wedge of lime.
-- The classic three-ingredient serve — the ratio of gin to tonic is really down to taste, but 1:3 is a good starting point.

drinks.title: Gin Basil Smash
drinks.history: Jörg Meyer created it at Le Lion and first called it the Gin Pesto. It is one of very few 21st-century drinks to enter the standard repertoire worldwide, and Meyer published the recipe openly rather than guarding it.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, sugar syrup and basil leaves hard with ice, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice.

drinks.title: Gin Daisy
drinks.history: The Daisy family — spirit, citrus, a sweetener and a splash of soda — is one of the oldest templates in the book, and the one the Margarita is most plausibly descended from.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, grenadine and cointreau hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Gin Fizz
drinks.history: Henry Ramos's version, made at the Imperial Cabinet Saloon from 1888, was shaken for twelve minutes and needed a relay of bartenders passing the tin down a line to keep up with demand.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a highball glass over fresh ice and top with soda water.
-- A "Ramos Gin Fizz" adds cream, egg white and orange flower water for a much richer version.

drinks.title: Gin Rickey
drinks.history: Made at Shoomaker's bar for Colonel Joe Rickey, a lobbyist, and originally built on bourbon. The gin version took over by the 1890s. It is the District of Columbia's official native cocktail.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice, add gin and the juice of lime, then top with soda water.
Drop the spent lime shell into the glass and stir.
-- Unsweetened by design — one of the few classics with no sugar in it at all.

drinks.title: Ginger Juice Syrup
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Select a good quantity of fresh root ginger for your needs (at least ginger).
Wash root ginger in hot water.
Chop root ginger, leaving skin on, into chunks that will fit into the intake of your juicer.
Use a centrifugal or masticating (cold press) juicer to extract ginger juice.
Place a saucepan on your scales and zero the scales.
Pour ginger juice into the saucepan and record its weight.
Pour caster sugar into the pan until double the original weight of ginger juice is reached — by weight, equal parts ginger juice to sugar.
Place pan on the hob and apply very low heat, just to gently warm.
Stir until all the sugar has dissolved, 5 minutes.
Fine strain into a sterilised bottle and seal.
Store in a refrigerator for up to 2 days.

drinks.title: Ginger Milk Tea (Adrak Chai)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Pour water into a pot and begin to heat it. Add ginger root, peeled and grated, and loose leaf tea. Bring to a rolling boil and let simmer on medium heat for 2-3 minutes until the chai turns dark.
Pour milk and bring to a boil on medium-high heat. Reduce the heat and bring it to a boil again on medium heat.
Reduce the heat completely and add organic sugar, ground cardamom, ground black pepper, and dried ground ginger (optional but recommended for extra healing properties and warmth).
Using a soup ladle, mix well and aerate the ginger milk tea 4 to 5 times. Turn off the heat and cover the pot.
Let rest for 3-4 minutes, then strain the ginger milk tea into serving cups and serve hot. — Limit to 1-2 cups per day to avoid dehydration

drinks.title: Ginger Tea Recipe (Fresh Ginger Root Tea)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Rinse ginger under running water. If required soak it in a bowl of water to loosen the mud deposits and scrub it well with a vegetable brush. Optionally peel the ginger with a table knife or a spoon, peeling only 2.5 cm and keeping the rest intact.

Bring water to a rolling boil. Meanwhile grate or chop the ginger. Add the ginger to the boiling water. If using optional spices and herbs like cinnamon, black pepper, or Tulsi leaves, add them at this step.
Simmer covered for 3-4 minutes. If using chopped or sliced ginger instead of grated, boil for 5-6 minutes.
When the ginger tea is ready you will see it turns to a light yellow color. Turn off the heat and strain to a serving cup. Press down with a spoon to extract most of the ginger flavor.

Stir in lemon juice (or lime juice, calamansi or grapefruit juice). If you want to sweeten it add honey when it cools down slightly — do not stir honey into very hot tea. If the tea is too spicy for your taste, simply dilute it with hot water.

drinks.title: Globetrotter
drinks.author: Lorenzo Antinori
steps: Stir bourbon, calvados, sweet vermouth, cherry heering, and orange bitters with a single large ice cube, then strain into a rock glass.
Garnish with orange twist and lemon twist. Add korean soy sauce or standard soy sauce.

drinks.title: Godfather
drinks.history: Scotch and amaretto, named after the 1972 film. Its relations follow the same joke — vodka makes it a Godmother, brandy a French Connection.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add scotch whisky and amaretto.
Stir gently.
-- Swap the scotch for vodka and it becomes a Godmother instead.

drinks.title: Godmother
drinks.history: The vodka counterpart to the Godfather, which is scotch and amaretto. Both names were attached after the 1972 film.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add vodka and amaretto.
Stir gently.
-- The vodka sibling of the Godfather, same simple two-ingredient build.

drinks.title: Gold Basque Punch
drinks.author: David Rios
steps: Build all ingredients in a punch bowl and stir to combine.
Johnnie Walker Gold Label Reserve Amer Picon pineapple juice grenadine soda water
Garnish with orange slices, star anise, and mint leaves.

drinks.title: Gold Rush
drinks.history: T.J. Siegal made it at Milk & Honey — a bourbon sour with honey syrup in place of sugar. Three ingredients, and one of the most copied drinks of the modern revival.
steps: Shake bourbon, lemon juice and honey syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a glass over fresh ice.
-- A modern classic from New York's Milk & Honey — effectively a Whiskey Sour with honey standing in for sugar.

drinks.title: Golden Cadillac
drinks.history: Created at Poor Red's, a tiny barbecue bar in the Gold Country, and named after a customer's car. The bar became one of the largest single buyers of Galliano in the world on the strength of it.
steps: Shake white crème de cacao, galliano and cream hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A sweet, custardy 1950s creation from a California steakhouse, named for the car in the parking lot.

drinks.title: Golden Dream
drinks.history: Built around Galliano, in the same wave of Italian-liqueur drinks that gave America the Harvey Wallbanger and the Golden Cadillac.
steps: Shake galliano, cointreau, orange juice and cream hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Goldfish in a Bag
drinks.author: Ian Cameron
steps: Add gin and mandarin vodka to a plastic ziplock bag.
Add rhubarb bitters to the bag.
Add a few cubes of ice to the bag, then seal it.
Top with tonic water from a small bottle.
Garnish with pink grapefruit zest cut in the shape of fish and edible lily pads.
Insert a straw through the bag and serve.

drinks.title: Grand Cosmopolitan
steps: Add vodka, cranberry juice, triple sec, and fresh lime juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well 10 seconds and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lime wheel.

drinks.title: Grape Crush Shot
drinks.history: Vodka, raspberry or grape liqueur and lemonade, named after the soda. One of the sweet shooters that no one claims and every bar could make.
steps: Shake vodka, raspberry liqueur and lemonade briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Grapefruit Paloma Cocktail
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: Pour kosher salt on a small plate. Rub the rim of the glass with a lime wedge or grapefruit wedge (make sure you don't add too much liquid to the rim), then dip the glass rim in the salt.
Place ice cubes in the glass.
Pour in tequila Patrón Silver, lime juice, and natural syrup or white sugar. Combine well.
Finally, add grapefruit juice, garnish with a wedge of lime or grapefruit, and enjoy your refreshing Paloma Cocktail!

drinks.title: Grappa Espresso Martini
steps: Chill a coupe glass with ice.
Add vodka, grappa, coffee liqueur, and freshly brewed espresso to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake vigorously for 10 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass and serve immediately with a layer of crema on top.

drinks.title: Grasshopper
drinks.history: Philibert Guichet of Tujague's created it for a New York cocktail competition, where it took second place. New Orleans still serves it, and Tujague's still claims it.
steps: Shake crème de menthe, crème de cacao and cream hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A dessert-in-a-glass classic from 1920s New Orleans, named for its bright mint-green colour.

drinks.title: Green Tea Shot
drinks.history: There is no tea in it. Whiskey, peach schnapps and sour mix happen to land close to the flavour, and the colour finishes the illusion.
steps: Shake whiskey, peach schnapps, lime juice and lemonade briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Grog
steps: Mix rum with water and lime juice in a glass. Stir well and serve.

drinks.title: Grog (British Navy Grog)
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Dilute rum with water at a ratio of 1 part rum to 4 parts water, mixing the spirits together in a serving vessel or scuttled butt (a fresh-water cask).
Add lime juice and sugar if desired, stirring well to combine. Serve in the traditional manner to sailors before noon or at the end of the working day.

drinks.title: Groseille (Redcurrant) Syrup
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Wash redcurrants while still on their stems.
Destalk your washed redcurrants by holding the stalk over a bowl and run a fork down the length of the sprig so the fork's tines strip the berries from the stem with a comb-like action.
Muddle the currants in the base of a saucepan to juice.
Cover muddled redcurrants with water.
Add white caster sugar.
Stir to mix three ingredients together.
Heat pan on a hob while stirring occasionally and bring to the boil.
Continue to boil for 5 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes continuing to stir.
Cover pan and leave to cool.
Strain through a fine sieve and then through a cheesecloth or 100 micron strainer.
