Add vodka to your syrup to help prevent it from jellifying. — The above should yield 400 mL syrup which should be refrigerated in a sanitised sealed bottle and used within 14 days. Even with the vodka, shake the bottle at least a couple of times a day to help prevent jellification.

drinks.title: Gummy Bear
drinks.history: Raspberry vodka and peach schnapps with lemonade. Flavoured vodkas arrived in force in the 2000s and this is what bars did with them.
steps: Shake vodka, raspberry liqueur, peach schnapps and pineapple juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Hangman's Blood
drinks.author: Anthony Burgess (as cited)
steps: Pour gin, whisky, rum, port and brandy into a pint glass.
Add stout and top up with champagne.
Stir well and serve.

drinks.title: Harvey Wallbanger
steps: Pour vodka and fresh orange juice into highball glass filled with ice cubes. Stir well to combine.
Float Galliano liqueur on top by pouring it slowly over the back of a bar spoon. Garnish with an orange slice.

drinks.title: Hazelnut Old Fashioned
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nutty, rich, sweet" — an Old Fashioned built on Buffalo Trace bourbon with crème de cacao and hazelnut standing in for the usual sugar, plus cacao bitters. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Stir Buffalo Trace bourbon, crème de cacao, hazelnut liqueur and cacao bitters with plenty of ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, then strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with an orange twist.
notes: Nutty, rich and sweet, per the bar's own menu — a dessert-leaning Old Fashioned, closer to a boozy Nutella than the classic bitters-and-sugar version.

drinks.title: Heart of Darkness
drinks.author: Courtney Colarik
steps: Add tequila blanco (Cimarrón Blanco), mezcal (Koch Espadin), lime juice, agave syrup, activated charcoal raspberry preserves, and Bittermens Mole bitters to a shaker with ice. Shake well and fine strain into a snifter filled with crushed ice.
Garnish with a black lace heart-shaped doily and an activated charcoal sprayed orchid on top.
Note: Activated charcoal raspberry preserves are made by mixing 1 jar (370 g) of raspberry preserves with 5 tsp of activated charcoal using an immersion blender.

drinks.title: Hemingway Daiquiri
drinks.history: Constantino Ribalaigua at El Floridita built it to Ernest Hemingway's specification: no sugar, because of his diabetes, and double the rum, because he was Hemingway. He called his the Papa Doble.
steps: Shake white rum, maraschino liqueur, grapefruit juice and lime juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- No added sugar at all — Hemingway reportedly preferred his daiquiris bone dry, on doctor's orders about his diabetes.

drinks.title: High Ryeser
steps: Pour whiskey and vermouth into a mixing glass with ice and stir well. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: High Ryeser Manhattan
steps: Add rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and angostura bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 30 seconds until chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a cherry.

drinks.title: Himitsu Cocktail
drinks.author: Kenichi Kakuta
steps: Shake vodka, vodka citroen, blackberry liqueur, yellow tomato juice, lemon juice, maple syrup, and marmite with ice and fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: Honolulu
drinks.author: Victor Bergeron
steps: Blend rum (Bacardi Superior), pineapple juice (fresh pressed), lemon juice (freshly squeezed), sugar syrup, and grenadine with a 12 oz scoop of crushed ice 1 minute until smooth and serve with straws.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge and maraschino cherry.

drinks.title: Horse's Neck
drinks.history: Originally a non-alcoholic soft drink of ginger ale and a long spiral of lemon peel — the peel, draped over the rim and down into the glass, was said to resemble a horse's neck and gave the drink its name. Brandy or bourbon was added later once it moved from soda fountains to bars.
steps: Peel a whole lemon in one long spiral and coil it around the inside of the glass before adding ice, so one end hangs over the rim.
Fill a Highball glass with ice, add bourbon and stir briefly. Top with ginger ale.
notes: The garnish is the whole point of the name — do not skip the long spiral peel for a plain lemon wedge, or it is just a bourbon and ginger ale.

drinks.title: Hot Buttered Rum
drinks.history: The colonies had cheap molasses and their own rum distilleries, both products of the triangular trade. Hot butter, sugar and spice turned it into a winter drink, and it was standard in taverns long before it was a treat.
steps: Add dark rum, brown sugar and butter to a warmed mug.
Top with hot water, stir until the butter melts, and finish with a pinch of cinnamon.

drinks.title: Hot Toddy
drinks.history: Toddy comes from tārī, the Hindi word for fermented palm sap. British drinkers applied it to hot spirit with sugar, water and spice, and Scotland in particular made it the standard remedy for a cold — which it is not, though it helps.
steps: Add whiskey, honey and lemon juice to a heatproof glass mug.
Top with hot water and stir until the honey dissolves.
Garnish with a lemon slice and a clove-studded slice if you like.
-- As much a cold remedy as a cocktail — versions of it have been used medicinally since the 1700s.

drinks.title: How to Juice Pomegranates Using a Lever Press
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Cut pomegranate in half around the equator.
Place halves cut side down in lever press.
Position container under the press to collect juice.
Squeeze pomegranates by pulling down on the press' lever. — Each ripe pomegranate yields approximately 60 mL of juice.
The strainer built into the pillar press should remove most of the bitter white pith, leaving rich red pomegranate juice in the container.

drinks.title: How to Use Fresh Passion Fruit in Cocktails
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Select heavy passion fruits as the light ones tend to be dried out and lacking in juice. The fruit should have thick, leathery skin that is yellowish-green or brownish-red in colour. Ripe fruits will have a pockmarked, almost wrinkly appearance.
Cut the passion fruit in half with a sharp knife and scoop the flesh out of the shell into your shaker. Alternatively, simply push the flesh out by squeezing the fruit half between your fingers.

If you are making a blended drink, pass the flesh through a sieve to strain out the seeds before combining it with other ingredients. For shaken drinks, this step is not necessary as the seeds will be removed when the drink is fine strained into the glass.

drinks.title: Hugo Spritz
drinks.history: Roland Gruber created it with lemon balm syrup; elderflower replaced it as the drink spread, and now dominates. It went from one Alpine village to the default summer drink of Austria, Germany and northern Italy in about a decade.
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add elderflower liqueur and top with prosecco and a splash of soda water.
Garnish with a sprig of mint and a slice of lime.
-- A lighter, drier alternative to the Aperol Spritz, popular in Italy and Austria.

drinks.title: Hurricane
drinks.history: Wartime shortages meant Pat O'Brien's on Bourbon Street had to buy cases of rum it did not want in order to get one case of whiskey it did. The Hurricane was invented to use the rum up, and served in a glass shaped like a hurricane lamp.
steps: Shake light rum, dark rum, passion fruit syrup, orange juice, lime juice and grenadine hard with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with a slice of orange and a maraschino cherry.
-- Born at Pat O'Brien's bar in New Orleans, originally created to shift surplus rum during a wartime spirits shortage.

drinks.title: Inception Negroni
drinks.author: Robyn Gray
steps: Prepare the ice sphere by placing it in a freezer at minus 6°C for 3.5 hours.
Using a drill bit warmed with hot water, carefully drill out the ice sphere and drain any water inside. Work carefully to avoid cracking the sphere.
Make the inner red Negroni to a modified ratio to keep it liquid when frozen: gin (Brokers), Campari and sweet vermouth. Pre-chill this mixture in the freezer until very cold.

Using a pour spout or syringe, carefully inject the pre-chilled red Negroni into the hollowed ice sphere. Cap the sphere with crushed ice and drip cold water on top with a bitters dasher to seal it. Return to the freezer for 30-60 minutes until fully frozen.
While the sphere freezes, prepare the white Negroni that will sit on top: combine Suze, Martini Bianco and gin (Brokers) and stir with ice.

Pour the white Negroni into a rocks glass, gently place the ice sphere in the glass, and garnish with a lemon twist. Serve and explain to the drinker that they can drink the white Negroni first, wait for the ice to crack and reveal the red Negroni inside, or crack the sphere early to mix both cocktails together.

drinks.title: Irani Chai Recipe (Hyderabadi Irani Tea)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Pour milk to a deep pot and add sugar. Bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat and let simmer until it reduces to half the quantity, approximately 10 minutes.

Optional— if you don't like layers of cream in your Irani chai, pull the milk as it boils. Take a ladle full of milk and pour it back to the pot. Repeat this a few times until the cream breaks down and the milk turns frothy.
Meanwhile, pour water to another pot and add black tea (loose tea leaves or dust). Crush green cardamoms well and add them to the pot.
Cover and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and let simmer (covered) for 7-8 minutes until the decoction reduces to about 250 ml. Strain the chai to a kettle.
When the milk has evaporated to half the quantity, turn off the heat.

Divide the chai among 2 to 3 serving cups and top with the thick milk. If you don't like cream, you can strain it or pull the milk first in the pot before pouring it into the cups. Adjust the ratio of chai to milk to suit your taste.
Serve Irani chai hot or warm with your favorite tea biscuits or cookies.

drinks.title: Irish Car Bomb
drinks.history: Charles Burke Cronin Oat created it at Wilson's Saloon. The name refers to the Troubles and is taken as a serious insult in Ireland, where bars that serve it call it an Irish Slammer instead.
steps: Layer irish cream and irish whiskey in a shot glass.
Drop into half a glass of stout and drink quickly before it curdles.

drinks.title: Irish Coffee
drinks.author: Joe Sheridan
steps: Warm an Irish whiskey glass and set aside. Heat strong black coffee in a kettle or pot until steaming hot.
Pour the hot coffee into the warmed glass, leaving room at the top for cream.
Add Irish whiskey to the coffee and stir well to combine.
Lightly whip heavy cream until it reaches a pourable but slightly thickened consistency — it should float on top of the coffee rather than sink.
Carefully pour the whipped cream over the back of a spoon onto the surface of the coffee so it floats as a layer on top.
Serve immediately and drink the hot coffee and whiskey through the cool layer of cream.

drinks.title: Irish Mule
drinks.history: The Moscow Mule template with Irish whiskey in place of vodka, part of the recent wave of national riffs on the same copper-mug format.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add irish whiskey and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir gently.
-- A whiskey riff on the Moscow Mule, built the same way.

drinks.title: ItaliCup
steps: Add Italicus rosolio and fresh lemon juice to a highball glass filled with ice cubes.
Top with soda water and stir gently.
Garnish with a lemon wheel or fresh mint sprig.

drinks.title: Jack Rose
drinks.history: Applejack, grenadine and lime — one of the few cocktails built on American apple brandy rather than an imported spirit. It turns up in Ernest Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises, ordered in a Paris bar in 1926.
steps: Shake apple brandy, lime juice and grenadine hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A Prohibition-era classic named for its rosy colour, built on applejack rather than the more usual gin or whiskey.

drinks.title: Jägerbomb
drinks.history: Jägermeister was a 56-herb digestif for older Germans until importer Sidney Frank reinvented it for American students in the 1980s. The drop shot followed Red Bull's US launch in 1997, and the two have been inseparable since.
steps: Pour jägermeister into a shot glass.
Drop the shot glass into a larger glass holding energy drink and drink straight away.

drinks.title: Japanese Cocktail
drinks.history: In Jerry Thomas's very first bar guide. Nothing in it is Japanese — the name is most likely a nod to the first Japanese diplomatic mission to the United States, which had passed through New York two years earlier.
steps: Stir cognac, orgeat and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Jelly Bean
drinks.history: Sambuca with blackberry brandy or grenadine, which together give the aniseed-and-fruit taste of the sweet.
steps: Pour sambuca and blackberry liqueur into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Jet Pilot
drinks.history: From the Luau, a descendant of Don the Beachcomber's Test Pilot. Three rums, falernum, cinnamon and absinthe — the kind of recipe that made tiki bars guard their spec sheets.
steps: Shake dark rum, overproof rum, lime juice, grapefruit juice, falernum and absinthe hard with ice, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice.

drinks.title: Jockey Club Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add dry gin, crème de noyau, lemon juice, sugar syrup, Angostura bitters, and orange bitters to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake vigorously 10 seconds and strain into a chilled coupe glass. — Reddy-pink coloured with a sweet and sour almondy amaretto-like flavour fortified by gin botanicals.

drinks.title: John Collins
drinks.history: Named for a head waiter at Limmer's Hotel in Mayfair and originally made with genever. When gin styles split, so did the drink: Old Tom gin made it a Tom Collins, and the John Collins ended up as the whiskey version.
steps: Shake whiskey, lemon juice and sugar syrup with ice.
Strain into a collins glass over ice and top with soda water.
-- The whiskey original that the gin-based Tom Collins was later adapted from.

drinks.title: Joy Division
steps: Pour gin and dry vermouth into a mixing glass with ice, stir well until chilled. Strain into a chilled coupe glass. Add triple sec and several dashes of absinthe. Stir gently to combine.

drinks.title: Jungle Bird
drinks.history: Created as the welcome drink at the Kuala Lumpur Hilton's Aviary Bar. It is the rare tiki drink built on something bitter — the Campari is what keeps the pineapple from cloying, and what made it a bartender favourite when it was rediscovered.
steps: Shake dark rum, campari, pineapple juice, lime juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a glass over fresh ice.
-- A tiki cocktail invented at the Kuala Lumpur Hilton, unusual for pairing bitter Campari with tropical juice.

drinks.title: Kamikaze
drinks.history: Generally said to have been mixed at an American naval base in postwar Japan, with the name borrowed — grimly — from the wartime pilots. It was a full-sized drink long before it became a shot.
steps: Shake vodka, triple sec and lime juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass or serve as a shot.
-- Equal parts of all three ingredients makes this one of the easiest classics to remember.

drinks.title: Kamikaze Shot
drinks.history: The full-sized Kamikaze cut down to a shot — equal parts vodka, triple sec and lime. It was one of the drinks that made shots a bar category in their own right.
steps: Shake vodka, triple sec and lime juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Kentucky Mule
drinks.history: Bourbon in place of the Moscow Mule's vodka, named for Kentucky's whiskey. One of several regional mules that followed the copper-mug format's revival.
steps: Fill a copper mug with ice.
Add bourbon and top with ginger beer. Garnish with a wedge of lime.
-- A Moscow Mule with bourbon standing in for the vodka.

drinks.title: Key Lime Pie
drinks.history: Vanilla vodka, lime and cream, after the Florida Keys dessert. The graham-cracker rim, when a bar bothers, is the part that sells it.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka, lime cordial, pineapple juice and cream briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: King Redeye
drinks.author: Jesse Vida
steps: Stir Havana Club 7, Carpano Antica Formula, Aperol, Galliano Ristretto, 1 dash absinthe and 1 dash aromatic bitters with ice and serve.

drinks.title: Kingston Negroni
drinks.history: Joaquín Simó's Negroni made with Jamaican pot-still rum in place of gin. The funk of the rum stands up to Campari in a way most substitutions do not.
steps: Stir dark rum, campari and sweet vermouth with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange twist.

drinks.title: Kir
drinks.history: Named for Canon Félix Kir — priest, Resistance member and mayor of Dijon — who served white burgundy with crème de cassis at civic receptions to promote both local products at once. Before him it was simply called blanc-cassis.
steps: Pour crème de cassis into a wine glass.
Top with chilled dry white wine and stir gently.
-- A simple Burgundian aperitif named after Canon Félix Kir, mayor of Dijon, who popularised the blend of blackcurrant liqueur and local white wine.

drinks.title: Kir Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour Bourgogne Aligoté white wine into a well-chilled glass, then add crème de cassis, and top with the remaining Bourgogne Aligoté white wine. Ensure all ingredients are well-chilled before serving — the key to a good Kir is the balance between the sweet cassis and the acidic white wine. Pour half the wine first, then the cassis, then the rest of the wine to help the ingredients combine well.

drinks.title: Kir Royale
steps: Pour crème de cassis into a champagne flute.
Top with champagne or other quality sparkling wine, stirring gently to combine.
Serve immediately as an elegant aperitif.

drinks.title: Knickerbocker Cocktail
steps: Pre-chill an old fashioned glass. Select and prepare a garnish of a spent (squeezed) half lime shell and seasonal berries such as raspberries, blackberries, or blueberries.
SHAKE light gold rum, Ferrand Dry Curaçao liqueur, Monin Raspberry Syrup, and lime juice with ice.
STRAIN into the glass filled 2/3 with cubed ice.
TOP up the glass with crushed ice.
Garnish with the lime shell and seasonal berries. Serve with a straw.

drinks.title: Kool-Aid Shot
drinks.history: Melon liqueur, raspberry liqueur and cranberry, named for the colour rather than any actual Kool-Aid.
steps: Shake vodka, melon liqueur, cranberry juice and amaretto briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: La Dame de Fer
drinks.author: Erik Lorincz
steps: Add Chateau Boulard Calvados, Trois Riviere Rhum, fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup, and leather-infused angostura bitters to a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake vigorously and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with matcha tea dust.

drinks.title: La Última Paloma
drinks.author: Diego González
steps: Add Patrón Silver, homemade grapefruit cordial, fresh lime juice, and celery bitters to a mixing tin.
Shake and strain into a coupe or wine glass.

drinks.title: Lassi Recipe (Sweet & Salt Lassi)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: For the sweet lassi version, chill yogurt and water in the refrigerator. If using saffron, soak saffron strands in 1 tsp of hot milk and let it rest.
Add the chilled yogurt to a large bowl and whisk well to break up lumps and make it smooth.
Add sugar, cardamom powder, rose water (optional) and the soaked saffron to the smooth yogurt. Whisk well until combined.
Pour the chilled water and whisk until very frothy. Taste test and add more water or sugar as needed. Transfer to serving glasses and garnish with chopped nuts (optional).

For the salted lassi version, dry roast cumin seeds on low heat until aromatic, then cool completely and powder finely. Whisk yogurt in a bowl. Add black salt (or to taste) and roasted cumin powder. Whisk everything well until smooth. Pour water and whisk again until frothy. Taste test and adjust salt or cumin as needed.

For the mint masala lassi, add yogurt, water, sugar (optional), salt (to taste), cumin powder, chaat masala, mint leaves, lemon juice, and green chili (optional, deseeded) to a blender. Blend until frothy and smooth. Pour to serving glasses and serve chilled.

drinks.title: Last Word
steps: Pour gin, green chartreuse, crème de maraschino, and fresh lime juice into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with maraschino cherries on a pick.

drinks.title: Le Frog
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add Islay single malt whisky, black raspberry liqueur and pineapple juice to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

drinks.title: Leather-Aged Cocktails (Unfinished Business)
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Pour Woodford Reserve bourbon, Martini Rosso, bitters, and galangal into a 40 litre leather wineskin — this is a long-term aging project, not a single serving cocktail.

Allow the mixture to age in the leather wineskin for several months, as the leather slowly imparts subtle flavor changes to the cocktail. The juniper-treated interior of the wineskin will gently influence the spirit without overpowering it with pine notes.
When ready to serve, pour the aged cocktail over a large ice ball in a rocks glass.
Serve alongside Spanish chorizo and caper berries to complement the rich, smooth character of the drink.

drinks.title: Lemon Drop
drinks.history: The shot form of Norman Jay Hobday's drink at Henry Africa's — sugared rim, lemon wedge, and the whole thing designed to taste like the boiled sweet.
steps: Rim the glass with sugar.
Shake vodka, triple sec and lemon juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Lemon Drop Martini
drinks.history: Norman Jay Hobday created it at Henry Africa's, the bar generally credited with inventing the fern bar — plants, stained glass and sweet drinks aimed at people who found classic cocktails forbidding. Named after the boiled sweet.
steps: Run a lemon wedge around the rim of a chilled glass and dip it in sugar to coat.
Shake vodka, triple sec, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into the glass.
-- Named for tasting like the boiled sweet — sharp, sweet and cold.

drinks.title: Lemon Meringue Shot
drinks.history: Limoncello or lemon vodka with a float of cream. Limoncello itself comes from the Amalfi coast, where it is drunk cold and neat rather than layered.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka, limoncello and cream briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Liquid Cocaine
drinks.history: Several unrelated recipes share the name — Jägermeister and Goldschläger, or 151 rum and peppermint. All of them are strong, which is the only thing the name reliably promises.
steps: Shake jägermeister, peppermint schnapps and overproof rum briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Long Beach Iced Tea
drinks.history: A Long Island with cranberry juice in place of the cola, which makes it red rather than tea-coloured and no weaker at all.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add vodka, gin, white rum, tequila, triple sec and lemon juice and stir briefly. Top with cranberry juice.

drinks.title: Long Island Iced Tea
drinks.history: Robert \"Rosebud\" Butt says he made it at the Oak Beach Inn as an entry in a triple sec competition. A rival claim points to a Prohibition-era drink from a different Long Island, this one in Kinston, Tennessee. There is no tea in it — the cola does that work.
steps: Shake vodka, gin, white rum, tequila, triple sec and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into a tall highball glass over ice and top with cola.
-- Despite the name there's no tea in it at all — the cola just makes it look like one.

drinks.title: Lucille's Winning COLD Cocktail
drinks.author: Lucille Carter
steps: Shake gin, lime juice, orgeat, maraschino, and grapefruit juice over ice and strain into an ice-filled glass. Top up with sparkling whole rosebud tea and garnish with a mint sprig.

drinks.title: Macca Margarita
steps: Pour tequila, triple sec, fresh lemon juice, and fresh orange juice into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled margarita glass rimmed with salt.
Garnish with a lime wheel or orange slice.

drinks.title: Mai Tai
drinks.history: Victor \"Trader Vic\" Bergeron's account: aged Jamaican rum, lime, orgeat and orange curaçao, handed to Tahitian friends who tasted it and said \"Maita'i roa ae\" — out of this world. Don the Beachcomber claimed a 1933 version, and the two men argued about it for decades.
steps: Shake white rum, dark rum, lime juice, orange curaçao and orgeat syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over crushed ice and garnish with mint and a lime wheel.
-- Trader Vic's original 1944 recipe used a 17-year-old Jamaican rum he never disclosed the brand of.

drinks.title: Mandarin Liqueur
steps: Wash the mandarin oranges under running water and dry them carefully with a clean cloth, then gently remove the peel.

After separating the fruit from the peels, cover the latter with pure alcohol. Let macerate for 5 days at room temperature covered with plastic wrap, in a cool place away from light. Remember to shake the mixture once a day. 5 days
After this time, prepare the syrup: pour the sugar and water into a saucepan, heat until it boils 5 minutes, then turn off and let cool completely.

Add the syrup to the mixture of peels and alcohol, mix well, and let it rest covered for about 10-20 days 10-20 days, always taking care to shake it once a day. After this time, the volume will be slightly reduced, and the color will be more intense.
At this point, filter the mixture to remove the peels and decant it into bottles. Your mandarin liqueur is ready to be enjoyed very cold!

drinks.title: Mango Lassi
drinks.author: Jamie Oliver
steps: Put plain yoghurt, milk, mango pulp and sugar into a blender. Blend 2 minutes, pour into glasses and serve. Feel free to try salt and cardamom seeds instead of sugar. Keeps refrigerated up to 24 hours.

drinks.title: Mango Lassi Recipe
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Rinse the mangoes and chill them for a few hours. Peel and cube them. This keeps your mango lassi cold after blending. (Skip this step if using canned mango pulp.)
Add mangoes chopped, yogurt cold plain yogurt, milk cold milk, cardamom powder, and sugar to a blender jar.
Blend until the mango lassi is super smooth. It should be thick yet of pouring consistency. 3 minutes
Taste test and add more sugar if you want it sweeter or more milk or ice if you prefer it thinner. If you want more mango flavor, add more mangoes and a splash of water.
Pour mango lassi to serving glasses. If you prefer it colder, refrigerate it for an hour.
Garnish with chopped nuts like unsalted pistachios, a pinch of saffron strands, and whipped cream if desired.

drinks.title: Manhattan
steps: Add whiskey, sweet vermouth and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well 10 seconds until chilled and diluted.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a cherry or orange zest.

drinks.title: Manhattan (Sweet)
steps: Stir whiskey, sweet vermouth, and angostura bitters with ice in a mixing glass until well chilled. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a cherry.

drinks.title: Marconi
steps: Build gin, Italian red bitter liqueur, and sweet vermouth in a glass with ice and stir well. Garnish with an orange twist or cherry if desired and savour.

drinks.title: Margarita
drinks.place: Mexico and the US border — disputed
drinks.history: At least three people have claimed it: Carlos "Danny" Herrera at Rancho La Gloria near Tijuana around 1938, Dallas socialite Margarita Sames in Acapulco in 1948, and a Juárez bartender called Danny Negrete. The dullest explanation is probably the true one — margarita is Spanish for daisy, and a Daisy is simply a spirit, citrus and orange liqueur, which is exactly what this is. The first printed recipe ran in Esquire in December 1953.
steps: Prepare the glass by wiping the rim with lime and then placing it upside down on a bed of salt so that the rim has a light covering all the way round.
Shake tequila, triple sec, fresh lime juice and plenty of ice hard in a shaker, then strain into the glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a lime wheel.
notes: Many people's fear of tequila quickly dissipates when combined with that sweet double combo of lime juice and triple sec.

drinks.title: Margaritas
drinks.place: Mexico and the US border — disputed
drinks.history: At least three people have claimed it: Carlos \"Danny\" Herrera at Rancho La Gloria near Tijuana around 1938, Dallas socialite Margarita Sames in Acapulco in 1948, and a Juárez bartender called Danny Negrete. The dullest explanation is probably the true one — margarita is Spanish for daisy, and a Daisy is simply a spirit, citrus and orange liqueur, which is exactly what this is. The first printed recipe ran in Esquire in December 1953.
drinks.author: Jamie Oliver
steps: Rim glasses with lime and salt.
Shake tequila, triple sec and lime juice with ice.
Strain into glasses.

drinks.title: Marianito
steps: This vermouth-based cocktail is traditionally made with Spanish vermouth but is equally delicious made with Italian rosso vermouth.
Mix vermouth with ice in a shaker and strain into a chilled glass.

drinks.title: Martinez
drinks.history: The sweet ancestor of the Martini. The town of Martinez, California claims it and has a plaque saying so; San Francisco says it was mixed at Jerry Thomas's bar for a man on his way to Martinez. It first appears in print in 1884.
steps: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino liqueur and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Martini with a Spot
steps: Pour gin and dry vermouth into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Stir well and strain into a chilled martini glass.
Add a spot of absinthe as a garnish on top — the "dot" that gives this martini its name.

drinks.title: Mary Pickford
drinks.history: Named for the silent film star, and said to have been mixed for her by the bartender Fred Kaufman while she was in Cuba — one of many Hollywood names attached to Havana drinks in the Prohibition years.
steps: Shake white rum, pineapple juice, grenadine and maraschino liqueur hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Created in 1920s Havana in honour of the silent-film star during a visit.

drinks.title: Masala Chai Recipe (Indian Masala Tea)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Crush green cardamoms (or ground cardamom), cloves (or ground cloves), cinnamon (or ground cinnamon), and peppercorn (or ground pepper, optional) in a mortar pestle or spice grinder until fine.

Heat water in a pot. Add the crushed spices, ginger (chopped or crushed, optional), and black tea leaves (or tea powder, or 3-4 tea bags). — Start with lower tea amount and add more after adding milk if needed.
Bring to a rolling boil on medium-high heat, then reduce to medium or low. Let the decoction simmer for 3 minutes until dark.
Pour full fat milk and add sugar to taste. — If using tea bags, remove them at this stage to avoid bitterness.
Bring to a rolling boil on medium-high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer until the chai turns dark, for 2 minutes. The chai should thicken and reduce to about 420 ml.

Turn off the heat. You will see a layer of cream on top. Optional: Aerate the masala chai for authentic chaiwallah taste. Using a soup ladle or measuring cup, pour the hot tea from a height of 30-45 cm back into the pot. Repeat this pulling motion 4-5 times until the cream layer breaks down and incorporates back into the chai.
Strain the masala chai into serving cups and serve hot or warm with biscuits or snacks.

drinks.title: Masala Chai Toddy
drinks.author: Maunika Gowardhan
steps: Add all the spices except the ginger to a pestle & mortar. Crush cinnamon stick (or cassia bark), green cardamom pods, cloves, and black peppercorns to a coarse mix and set aside.
In a saucepan bring water to a boil. Add tea bags along with the crushed spices and ginger roughly crushed. Simmer for 7-8 minutes.
Add condensed milk and stir well followed by dark rum. Simmer for 1 minute.
Using a fine sieve strain the masala chai toddy into little glasses. Serve warm.

drinks.title: Matador
drinks.history: Tequila with pineapple and lime, from the run of postwar American tequila drinks that arrived alongside tiki. Simple, and older than most people assume.
steps: Shake tequila, pineapple juice and lime juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A simpler, older cousin of the Margarita, built entirely around tequila and pineapple.

drinks.title: Melon Ball
drinks.history: Midori, vodka and pineapple, created in the push behind Midori's American launch. The name is the garnish it was originally served with.
steps: Shake vodka, melon liqueur and pineapple juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Mexican Mule
drinks.history: A Moscow Mule with tequila. The mule template proved endlessly re-baseable, and this is the version that stuck alongside the original.
steps: Fill a Copper mug with ice, add tequila and lime juice and stir briefly. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with a lime wedge.

drinks.title: Mezcal Margarita
drinks.history: Mezcal's export boom after 2000 put a smoky margarita on nearly every list. Mezcal is not a style of tequila but its parent category — tequila is simply mezcal made from blue agave in a defined region.
steps: Rim the glass with salt.
Shake mezcal, cointreau and lime juice hard with ice, then strain into a Margarita glass.

drinks.title: Michelada
drinks.history: A staple of Mexican beer culture with countless regional variations — the name is popularly, if not definitively, traced to "mi chela helada" ("my cold beer"), and the drink is treated as much as a hangover cure as a refreshment in the heat.
steps: Salt the rim of a highball glass, then fill with ice. Add lime juice, a few dashes of hot sauce, a dash of Worcestershire sauce and a pinch of salt and black pepper. Top with cold lager and stir gently.
notes: Recipes vary enormously by region and household — clamato (tomato-clam juice) is a common addition in some versions, making it closer to a beer-based Bloody Mary.

drinks.title: Michelada Cocktail
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: Chill two tall beer glasses in the freezer for at least 60 minutes. Rim the edges of the glasses with a lime wedge, then turn the glasses upside down to dip first into salt and then into Tajin powder, coating the rims evenly. You can also mix the salt and Tajin together to make a single mixture.
Add ice cubes (about 4-5 cubes) to each glass.

Pour lime juice, Maggi sauce, Tabasco sauce, and Worcestershire sauce into each glass. Mix well with a spoon. Alternatively, you can mix all four ingredients in a small bowl and pour them evenly between the glasses.
Open Mexican lager beer (one beer per glass) and slowly pour it into each glass. Tilt the glass at a 45-degree angle when pouring to prevent too much foam.
Stir gently and garnish with a lime wedge. Serve immediately and enjoy!

drinks.title: Midnight Sun Cocktail
drinks.author: Ludde Grenmo
steps: Shake Hennessy VS, Cherry Heering, Coffee Heering, Madeira wine, caramelized filmjölk, and Epice riche extract with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and finish with freshly cracked black pepper.
For the caramelized filmjölk: combine equal parts filmjölk or yoghurt and caster sugar. Sous vide at 85°C for 20 hours.
For the Epice riche extract: steep ground nutmeg, cloves, white peppercorns, and allspice in vodka. Let sit for 10 hours.

drinks.title: Midori Sour
drinks.history: Suntory launched Midori at a party at Studio 54 for the cast of Saturday Night Fever. The sour is the drink that carried it through the 1980s, and the colour is the whole reason it sold.
steps: Shake melon liqueur, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice, then strain into a Highball glass over fresh ice. Top with soda water.

drinks.title: Milk Punch
drinks.author: The London EDITION's Punch Room
steps: Add pineapple, cloves, coriander seeds, angelica spice, allspice, and star anise to a pan. Pour in lemon sherbet, Batavia Arrack, applejack, Woodford Reserve, Raretea Green Tea, and lemon juice. Add boiling water, cover and let rest for at least 6 hours.

While the batch rests, simmer full fat milk in a separate pan until hot — this is important as the heat allows the milk proteins to curdle when the acidity of the punch base causes them to attract each other.
Add the hot milk to the rested batch and let it curdle. Filter through a super-bag to eliminate most of the solids.
Refrigerate the mixture, then filter it through a coffee filter, ideally twice. Store in a glass bottle in the fridge until ready to serve. — The batch makes 5 litres (34 drinks)
Garnish with edible flowers and pineapple leaf when serving.

drinks.title: Mimosa
drinks.history: Credited to the Hôtel Ritz and named for the yellow mimosa flower. London's Buck's Fizz, created at Buck's Club in 1921, is the same idea with twice the juice.
steps: Add orange juice to a chilled champagne flute.
Top with champagne, pouring slowly to preserve the fizz.
-- A brunch staple invented at the Ritz Paris in the 1920s, named for the mimosa flower it resembles in colour.

drinks.title: Mint Julep
steps: Bash up some ice and add to a julep cup.
Add bourbon whiskey, fresh mint leaves, sugar, and water to the cup.
Stir well and top with more ice to fill the cup.
Garnish with a sprig of fresh mint and serve super-cold. — The drink is not the same if it melts

drinks.title: Mixed Berry Smash
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — raspberry, blackberry and blueberry muddled with lime and sugar, lengthened with soda water, in the same smash format as a whiskey smash. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Muddle a handful of raspberries, blackberries and blueberries with sugar and lime juice in the base of a highball glass until the berries break down. Fill with ice and top with soda water. Stir gently and garnish with extra berries and a lime wheel.
notes: As fruity and full of pulp as a smash should be — leave the muddled berries in the glass rather than straining them out.

drinks.title: Mojito
steps: Gently muddle fresh mint leaves with lime juice and sugar in a highball glass to release the mint oils without crushing the leaves.
Fill the glass with crushed ice.
Pour white rum over the ice and stir well to combine.
Top with soda water and stir gently.
Garnish with a sprig of fresh mint and a lime wheel.

drinks.title: Monkey Gland
drinks.author: Harry MacElhone
steps: Pour gin and absinthe into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Add grenadine and shake vigorously until well chilled, approximately 10 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve immediately.

drinks.title: Moonshine Martini
drinks.author: Harry Craddock
steps: Stir gin and dry vermouth together with ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with an olive or lemon twist.

drinks.title: Moscow Mule
drinks.history: Mixed at the Cock 'n' Bull on Sunset Strip to shift three sets of unsold stock at once — Smirnoff vodka nobody wanted, house ginger beer that wasn't selling, and a consignment of copper mugs. It is widely credited with starting America's taste for vodka.
steps: Fill a copper mug with ice, then add vodka and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir gently.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
-- Traditionally served in a copper mug, which keeps the drink colder for longer and frosts on the outside.

drinks.title: Mountain Man Cocktail
steps: Add whisky, peach liqueur, fresh lemon juice, and ginger syrup to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a peach slice or twist of lemon.

drinks.title: Mudslide
steps: Pour vodka, kahlua, and baileys into a glass filled with ice.
Stir well and serve.

drinks.title: Mulled Cider
drinks.history: The cider-country cousin of mulled wine, from the orchards of the West Country. It shares its ancestry with wassail, the spiced-cider ritual of drinking to the health of the apple trees in midwinter.
steps: Combine the dry cider or fresh apple juice, apples, cinnamon sticks, allspice berries, orange zest, and dark rum (optional) in a large saucepan and simmer gently for 30 minutes - do not boil.
Transfer to a heatproof bowl and ladle into glass mugs. Garnish with apple to serve.
-- Clove-studded apples, spices, citrus and dark rum make this mulled cider recipe impossible to resist on a cold day; a great Christmas party drink.

drinks.title: Mulled Wine
drinks.history: The Romans heated and spiced wine as conditum paradoxum and carried the habit wherever the legions went. Germany's Glühwein, the Nordic glögg and Britain's Christmas mulled wine are all descendants of the same idea.
steps: Gently warm red wine with sugar, a couple of orange and a cinnamon stick — do not let it boil.
Ladle into a warmed mug, leaving the spices behind.

drinks.title: My Cherry Amore
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "bold, warming, smooth" — a Manhattan built on cherry-infused Buffalo Trace bourbon and Carpano Antica Formula sweet vermouth, with bitters. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Stir cherry-infused Buffalo Trace bourbon, Antica Formula sweet vermouth and angostura bitters with plenty of ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a cherry.
notes: Bold, warming and smooth, per the bar's own menu — a Manhattan for someone who wants the cherry garnish built straight into the spirit rather than left floating on top.

drinks.title: Naked & Famous
drinks.author: Joaquín Simó
steps: Pour mezcal, yellow chartreuse, dry vermouth, and yellow chartreuse into a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass. Serve up.

drinks.title: Naked and Famous
drinks.history: Joaquín Simó created it at Death & Co — an equal-parts descendant of the Last Word and the Paper Plane, built on mezcal. Four ingredients, all in equal measure, in the tradition it comes from.
steps: Shake mezcal, aperol, yellow chartreuse and lime juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A smoky modern classic built on four equal parts, first poured at New York's Death & Co.

drinks.title: Navy Grog
drinks.history: Don the Beachcomber's. Grog was the Royal Navy's watered rum ration, named after Admiral Edward Vernon and the grogram cloak he wore. The original is served over a cone of ice frozen around a straw.
steps: Shake dark rum, white rum, overproof rum, lime juice, grapefruit juice and honey syrup hard with ice, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice.

drinks.title: Negroni
drinks.history: Count Camillo Negroni is said to have asked barman Fosco Scarselli at Caffè Casoni to stiffen his Americano with gin in place of the soda. Family records suggest the Count had spent years in America as a gambler and rodeo rider before returning to Florence, which is the sort of detail that makes the story worth believing.
steps: Combine one part gin, one part vermouth, and one part Campari into a mixing glass with ice and stir until the glass begins to feel chilled. Strain into a tumbler and garnish with a slither of orange peel.
-- A perfectly balanced cocktail beloved by barmen worldwide. Although simple, always opt for the best quality spirits and aim for a sphere of ice rather than cubes.

drinks.title: Negroni Sbagliato
drinks.history: Sbagliato means mistaken: Mirko Stocchetto at Bar Basso reached for sparkling wine instead of gin while making a Negroni and served it anyway. Fifty years later a ten-second interview clip of Emma D'Arcy ordering one made it a global drink overnight.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add campari and sweet vermouth.
Top with prosecco instead of gin and stir gently.
Garnish with an orange slice.
-- "Sbagliato" is Italian for "mistaken" — the story goes a bartender grabbed prosecco instead of gin by accident.

drinks.title: New York Sour
drinks.history: A whiskey sour with a float of red wine. Despite the name it first appears in Chicago, as the Continental Sour — the New York label was attached decades later.
steps: Float a spoon of red wine over the top to finish.
Shake bourbon, lemon juice, sugar syrup and egg white hard with ice, then strain into a Rocks glass.

drinks.title: Nightjar - Ketel One Pot and Kettle
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Add Ketel One vodka, Ketel One genever, ginger beer, white style beer, Dutch ale, freshly squeezed lemon juice (from lemon), malted barley syrup, honey syrup, and Bitter Truth Aromatic Bitters to the copper kettle.
Stir well and serve in the copper kettle with tea cups on the side for sharing among up to eight people.

drinks.title: Nutty Irishman
drinks.history: Irish cream with hazelnut liqueur, served as a shot or stirred into coffee. Baileys launched in 1974 and half the shots of the following decade were built on it.
steps: Pour irish cream and hazelnut liqueur into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Oatmeal Cookie
drinks.history: Butterscotch schnapps, Irish cream and cinnamon. Another of the dessert shooters, and one of the closest to actually tasting like what it claims.
steps: Shake irish cream, butterscotch schnapps and cinnamon schnapps briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
drinks.history: Phil Ward created it at Death & Co: reposado tequila split with mezcal, agave in place of sugar, and a flamed orange twist. It is generally credited with starting the wave of mezcal cocktails that followed.
steps: Stir tequila, mezcal, agave syrup and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange twist.

drinks.title: Ode to Violet
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — one of the bar's own bartender recommendations, described there as "floral, niche". Built like an Aviation with a double measure of gin and an egg white for body, it leans further into the crème de violette than most, letting the perfume lead. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Dry shake Boatyard double gin, crème de violette, St Germain elderflower liqueur, lemon juice and egg white without ice first to build the foam, then shake again hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
notes: Floral and a little niche, as the bar's own menu puts it — closer to a perfume counter than a fruit bowl. Worth trying before dismissing the violette as too much; the lemon and gin keep it from tipping into potpourri.

drinks.title: Old Cuban
drinks.history: Audrey Saunders created it at the Carlyle Hotel — a Mojito crossed with a champagne cocktail, using aged rum and mint. One of the drinks that defined the New York revival.
steps: Shake aged rum, lime juice, sugar syrup, mint leaves and angostura bitters hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass. Top with champagne.

drinks.title: Old Fashioned
drinks.history: A cocktail was defined in print in 1806 as spirits, sugar, water and bitters — nothing more. By the 1880s bartenders were mixing fancier things, so drinkers who wanted the original started asking for it the old-fashioned way, and the name stuck to the drink. The Pendennis Club in Louisville claims to have made it famous.
steps: Add a teaspoon of caster sugar to a rocks glass with a few splashes of Angostura Bitters and a splash of hot water or soda water to dissolve the sugar. Stir until all of the sugar has dissolved and add a few ice cubes and one part whisky. Stir for 1 minute before topping up with ice and an orange peel or slice to garnish.
-- Works well with both bourbon and scotch. Originally invented to disguise bootleg whisky, with the bitters and sugar bringing out the sweetness of the spirit.

drinks.title: Old Fashioned Cocktail
drinks.author: Difford's Guide
steps: Add sugar and bitters to a rocks glass. Muddle gently to combine.
Add whiskey and water to the glass, then stir well to combine.
Add ice and stir until chilled. Garnish with a lemon or cherry.

drinks.title: Old Pal
steps: Stir rye whiskey, cognac, and dry vermouth with ice until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve.

drinks.title: Oleo Saccharum (Citrus Oil Syrup)
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Buy preferably organic unwaxed lemons (or other citrus fruit such as oranges, blood oranges, or grapefruit). Lemon works best in oleo-saccharum but oranges are often combined with lemon.
Wash your citrus fruit thoroughly.
Peel unwaxed lemons with as little of the white pith as possible and place peels in a Mason or Kilner jar. (If using 4 lemons then a 1 pint/500ml jar is plenty large enough.)
Measure caster sugar per lemon used and pour into the jar to cover lemon peels. For 4 lemons, use caster sugar.
Seal jar, shake well and leave overnight 12 hours. Occasional stirring helps extract the oils.

The clear citrus oil syrup found floating on top of the sugar in your jar the next day is pure oleo-saccharum. To dissolve the remaining sugar and extend your oleo-saccharum, add the same volume of lemon juice (or other citrus used) as you did caster sugar in step 4.

Reseal jar and shake until sugar has dissolved completely. You now have an oleo-saccharum shrub. If making a punch, pour this into your punch bowl, peels and all. Otherwise refrigerate until required and store for up to four days.

**Alternative method (with vacuum sealer):** Muddle citrus peels with caster sugar in a bowl. Pour muddled peels and sugar into vacuum bag, remove air and seal. Leave to infuse 12 hours at room temperature for the sugar to leach out and absorb the citrus oils. Date and refrigerate the sealed bag until required (within a week).

drinks.title: Optimist
steps: Add white rum, fresh lime juice, simple syrup to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lime wheel or twist if desired.

drinks.title: Orange Shrub
drinks.author: Tim Oakley
steps: To rum (preferably Bajan 40% abv.), add the juice and rind from oranges, just the rind of lemons and cinnamon stick, and store for around 3 days.
Remove cinnamon, add caster sugar and overproof rum, then bottle. Leave for at least 1 week in a cool place, shaking occasionally to dissolve all the sugar. — Makes approximately 2 × 700ml bottles

drinks.title: Orgeat Syrup
drinks.author: Jerry Thomas
steps: Drop sweet almonds and bitter almonds into boiling water. Let them stand until nearly cold, then peel them by pressing through your fingers.

Put the peeled almonds into a clean marble mortar and mash them thoroughly. Squeeze in the juice of lemon or add a little acid, and as you pound the almonds, pour water into the mortar; mash until the mixture looks like thick milk with no pieces of almonds remaining.

Add another water and squeeze the white mash through a hair-cloth or fine strainer, catching the liquid in a clean basin. Put any almond solids remaining in the cloth back into the mortar, mash again with a little more water, then strain and mix with the former almond milk.

Mix sugar which must first be clarified and boiled to "crack" stage. While adding the almond milk, keep the pan of hot sugar off the fire. Once mixed, give the syrup another boil up, then remove from heat and stir until cold.

Pour in a small portion of orange flower water or a few drops of essence of neroli. Pass the mixture through a cloth one final time. Bottle and shake occasionally for a few days to prevent the syrup from separating.

drinks.title: Oriental Treasure
drinks.author: Carla Molina Ruiz

ingredients.name: coconut water infused with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves

steps: Shake Opihr Oriental Spiced Gin, Arrack, lime juice, coconut water infused with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, palm sugar syrup — (1:1 palm sugar / coconut water), Good Luck bitters, and egg white with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass and garnish with a spray of the palm sugar syrup if desired.

drinks.title: Painkiller
drinks.place: Jost Van Dyke, British Virgin Islands
drinks.history: Daphne Henderson's Soggy Dollar Bar, so named because there is no dock and you swim ashore with your money in your pocket. Pusser's Rum later trademarked the name and sued a New York bar over it in 2011.
steps: Shake dark rum, pineapple juice, orange juice and coconut cream hard with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass over crushed ice and dust with grated nutmeg.
-- Invented at the Soggy Dollar Bar in the British Virgin Islands, reachable only by swimming ashore.

drinks.title: Paloma
steps: Add tequila, fresh grapefruit juice, and fresh lime juice to a glass filled with ice.
Top with soda water and stir gently.
Garnish with a grapefruit wedge and a pinch of sea salt on the rim if desired.

drinks.title: Papa's Fairground Old Fashioned
drinks.author: Simon Crompton

ingredients.name: Johnnie Walker Gold Label Reserve Blended Scotch Whisky
Talisker 10 year-old Single Malt Scotch Whisky

steps: Build in glass, adding the bitters and syrup to the glass first, then alternately adding cubes of ice and whisky, stirring all the time.
Top with a spray of Talisker over the surface of the drink and garnish with toasted marshmallows.

Ingredients: Johnnie Walker Gold Label Reserve Blended Scotch Whisky, Talisker 10 year-old Single Malt Scotch Whisky, Angostura Bitters, Popcorn-flavoured vodka apple pimento syrup, toasted marshmallows for garnish.

drinks.title: Paper Plane
drinks.history: Sam Ross created it at Milk & Honey in New York for the opening list of The Violet Hour in Chicago, and named it after the M.I.A. song. Four equal parts, in the Last Word tradition.
steps: Shake equal parts bourbon, aperol, amaro nonino and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A modern classic from 2007, named after the M.I.A. song.

drinks.title: Patrón Perfectionist
drinks.author: Joshua Garthwaite
steps: Combine Patrón Añejo, grapefruit juice, lemon juice, simple syrup, vanilla pod, black pepper, and cardamom oleo in a shaker.
Shake and double strain into a chilled coupe.
Spray Castle milk stout beer foam on top of the cocktail.
Garnish with dehydrated grapefruit and grapefruit dust.

drinks.title: Patrón Perfectionist - Li Tong
drinks.author: Li Tong
steps: To make the chamomile yuzu shrub: combine several pinches of dried chamomile, yuzu puree, sugar, apple cider vinegar, and water.
Add Patrón Reposado, Yellow Chartreuse, Chamomile yuzu shrub, Passionfruit syrup, and Lime juice to a Boston shaker.
Add ice to the shaker and shake well.
Strain into a Nick and Nora glass.
Top with Soda water.

drinks.title: Patrón Perfectionist - Overseas Milky Punch
drinks.author: Nathalie Durrieu

ingredients.name: homemade spices syrup (tonka, nutmeg, cinnamon, pepper, clove and vanilla)

steps: Combine Patrón Reposado, homemade horchata (rice and coconut milk), homemade spices syrup (tonka, nutmeg, cinnamon, pepper, clove and vanilla), Triple Sec, and Mezcal with ice in a shaker tin.

Using the Cuban roll technique, strain the ingredients into a second tin and then pour back into the first tin with ice. Repeat until ingredients are mixed and aerated, using longer pours each time you pass between shakers.
Pour into a glass to serve. Garnish with black sesame for garnish.

drinks.title: Pear & Elderflower Spritz
drinks.history: A house spritz from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "fruity, light, crisp" — Poire Williams pear brandy and St Germain elderflower liqueur lengthened with prosecco, in the same built-over-ice, topped-last format as an Aperol Spritz. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with ice, then add Poire Williams and St Germain elderflower liqueur and stir briefly. Top with prosecco, poured gently so it doesn't lose its fizz. Garnish with a thin pear slice.
notes: Fruity, light and crisp, as the bar's own menu puts it — an easy-drinking spritz for anyone who finds Aperol too bitter.

drinks.title: Pear Shaped
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — apple juice, pear purée, lime juice and passionfruit shaken together, no spirit at all. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake apple juice, pear purée, lime juice and the pulp of passionfruit hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a highball glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a thin pear slice.
notes: Named for the pun as much as the pear — a fruity, fully non-alcoholic option that doesn't taste like an afterthought.

drinks.title: Pegu Club
drinks.history: Named for the Pegu Club, an expatriate officers' club in colonial Rangoon, Burma. It appeared in print in Harry MacElhone's 1920s books (sources differ between 1923 and 1927) and was revived by Audrey Saunders at her New York bar of the same name.
steps: Shake gin, orange curaçao, lime juice, Angostura bitters and orange bitters hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a lime peel.
notes: Based on the common 2 oz / 3/4 oz / 1/2 oz build. Punch calls it very dry and suggests a dash of simple syrup if wanted; Difford's adds lime cordial and sugar syrup instead.

drinks.title: Penicillin
drinks.history: Sam Ross at Milk & Honey: blended scotch with honey and fresh ginger, and a float of peated Islay whisky on top so the smoke hits before the drink does. Probably the most successful cocktail of the 2000s.
steps: Shake blended scotch, lemon juice and honey-ginger syrup with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice, then float smoky islay scotch on top.
Garnish with a candied ginger piece.
-- Created by Sam Ross in New York in 2005, now one of the most-ordered modern classics worldwide.

drinks.title: Penicillin Cocktail
drinks.author: Sam Ross
steps: Build scotch whisky, peated Islay whisky, honey syrup, and fresh lemon juice in a cocktail shaker with ice. Shake well and strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish with a candied ginger slice.

drinks.title: Peppermint Patty
drinks.history: Peppermint schnapps with chocolate liqueur, named after the American mint chocolate. Frequently served hot in ski bars, which is where it makes most sense.
steps: Shake peppermint schnapps, crème de cacao and cream briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Perfect Manhattan
drinks.history: The favourite story — that it was invented at the Manhattan Club for a banquet thrown by Winston Churchill's mother, Jennie Jerome — cannot be true, since she was in England at the time, pregnant with Winston. It turns up in New York bar guides from the mid-1880s with no such fanfare.
steps: Stir rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, dry vermouth and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with lemon peel.
-- The Manhattan with the vermouth split evenly between sweet and dry, balancing the drink's richness.

drinks.title: Pickleback
drinks.history: At the Bushwick Country Club, bartender Reggie Cunningham took a customer's suggestion and chased a shot of Old Crow with the brine from the bar's pickle jar. The brine's salt and acid cancel the burn almost completely.
steps: Pour whiskey into a shot glass.
Drink it, then chase immediately with a shot of pickle brine.

drinks.title: Piedra Mayahuel
drinks.author: Jose Arturo Romero Venegas
steps: Add Patrón Silver, aged grapefruit liqueur, lemon juice, grapefruit soda, lechuguilla juice, and piloncillo & chicatanas agave syrup to the shaker with ice.
Shake until chilled and combined 10 seconds.
In a volcanic stone glass, pile frappé ice with a peak in the center like a snow cone.
Strain the cocktail over the ice in the glass, finishing with a dash of bitters and a delicate spray of chamomile and sage perfume.
Garnish with dehydrated grapefruit and flower. — Rim the glass with xoconostle salt if desired.

drinks.title: Pimm's and Other Bottled Fruit Cups
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour Pimm's No. 1 Cup or other bottled fruit cup over ice in a tall glass.
Dilute generously with English-style lemonade or ginger ale.
Garnish with citrus fruit slices, strawberries, and English cucumber slices, along with sprigs of borage or mint.
Serve immediately.

drinks.title: Piña Colada
steps: Combine white rum, pineapple juice, and cream of coconut in a blender with 1 handful of crushed ice.

Blend until smooth and pour into a chilled glass. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry. — For a lighter, less sweet version, use less cream of coconut or add a dash of pot still or agricole rum for extra body

drinks.title: Piña Colada (Difford's recipe)
drinks.author: Difford's
steps: Add white rum, pineapple juice, and coconut cream to a blender with 1 handful of crushed ice.
Blend until smooth and pour into a chilled glass, then garnish with a pineapple wedge.

drinks.title: Pink Gin
drinks.history: Angostura bitters were carried aboard as a stomach remedy, and officers took theirs in Plymouth gin. It was the wardroom drink of the Navy for well over a century.
steps: Stir gin and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice.

drinks.title: Pink Gin Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add gin to a glass primed with Angostura bitters. Swirl to coat the inside of the glass and add ice. Top with water and stir well. Add sugar.

drinks.title: Pink Lady
drinks.history: Named after a hit Broadway musical of 1911. It is a proper gin sour with applejack and egg white, but by the 1950s it had been recast as a ladies' drink, which is why serious bars stopped making it for forty years.
steps: Shake gin, applejack, grenadine, lemon juice and egg white hard without ice for 15 seconds to froth.
Add ice and shake again, then strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A Jazz Age classic named for its rosy hue, said to have been created for a hit Broadway play of the same name.

drinks.title: Pink Squirrel
drinks.history: From Bryant's Cocktail Lounge. Crème de noyaux, made from stone fruit kernels, supplies both the almond flavour and the pink.
steps: Shake crème de noyaux, crème de cacao and cream hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Piscola
steps: Pour pisco into a highball glass filled with ice.
Top with coca cola.
Stir and serve.

drinks.title: Pistache Fizz
drinks.author: Sean Muldoon and Jack McGarry
steps: Add pistachio milk, brandy, dry vermouth, lemon juice, and egg white to a shaker. Shake well 10 seconds without ice to emulsify the egg white, then add ice and shake vigorously 15 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and top with soda water to create a fizz. Garnish with a few pistachios on top.

drinks.title: Planter's Punch
drinks.history: Carried in a rhyme that is also the recipe: one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak. It reached New York print by 1908.
steps: Shake dark rum, orange juice, pineapple juice, lime juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a tall highball glass over crushed ice, dash angostura bitters on top, and garnish with fruit.
-- Old rhyme for the ratio: "one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak."

drinks.title: Poinsettia
steps: Pour champagne into a champagne_flute and top with cranberry_juice to create a festive red cocktail inspired by the poinsettia flower.

drinks.title: Popster
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Combine butterscotch schnapps, sweet and salty popcorn, and ice cream in a blender with 1/2 scoop of crushed ice and blend until smooth. Pour into a wine glass and top with popcorn as garnish.

drinks.title: Pornstar Martini
drinks.history: Douglas Ankrah created it at LAB in Soho and first called it the Maverick Martini, after a Cape Town club. The shot of prosecco alongside is part of the drink, not a garnish. It is now the most-ordered cocktail in Britain.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka, passion fruit puree, lime juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass, and serve with a shot of chilled prosecco on the side.
-- A modern classic devised by London bartender Douglas Ankrah in the 1990s, always served with its signature fizz chaser.

drinks.title: Prairie Fire
drinks.history: Tequila with a heavy dose of hot sauce. A dare shot rather than a drink, and a standing feature of American bar bets.
steps: Pour tequila and hot sauce into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Punch Romaine (Palate Cleanser)
steps: Whisk egg white with a dash of powdered sugar or syrup until it forms soft peaks (a loose meringue).
In a shaker with ice, shake white rum, dry white wine, fresh lemon juice, fresh orange juice, and simple sugar syrup until thoroughly chilled 1 minutes.
Pour the slushy mixture into a small coupe glass, top with Champagne, and spoon the frothy meringue over the top.

drinks.title: Purple Hooter
drinks.history: Vodka, raspberry liqueur and lime. Part of the run of brightly coloured shooters that American bars turned out through the decade; no creator is recorded.
steps: Shake vodka, raspberry liqueur and lime juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Purple Nurple
drinks.history: Vodka, blue curaçao and cranberry, which combine to purple. Another colour-first shooter of the era, with no origin on record.
steps: Shake vodka, raspberry liqueur, blue curaçao and lemonade briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Quelle Vie
drinks.author: Harry Craddock
steps: Add brandy and kummel to a mixing glass with ice and stir until well chilled. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.

drinks.title: Ramos Chocolate Fizz
steps: Shake gin, crème de cacao, heavy cream, vanilla extract, egg white, lemon juice, and simple syrup vigorously with ice until foamy.
Strain into a glass filled with ice and top with soda water, creating a thick foamy head characteristic of this creamy, chocolatey vanilla-fudge cocktail.

drinks.title: Ray Barrientos Cocktail
drinks.author: Thanos Prunarus
steps: Shake extra anejo rum, fresh lime juice, Cherry Heering, cinnamon syrup, fresh orange juice, and Angostura aromatic bitters well with ice. Reverse dry shake (shake again with no ice) and double strain into a cocktail glass.
Add methylcellulose to create a layer on top, then garnish with cinnamon stick and cherry.
-- For the cinnamon syrup: combine sugar and water in a 1:1 ratio with about cinnamon sticks per litre. Boil on low heat for 10 minutes then leave to rest.

drinks.title: Red Lion Cocktail
drinks.author: Arthur Albert Tarling
steps: Shake gin, lime juice, and Grand Marnier with ice vigorously 10 seconds until well chilled.
Rim a coupe glass with caster sugar and strain the cocktail into it. Serve immediately.

drinks.title: Redheaded Slut
drinks.history: Jägermeister, peach schnapps and cranberry. One of the Jägermeister shooters that came out of Sidney Frank's American campus marketing.
steps: Shake jägermeister, peach schnapps and cranberry juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Remember the Maine
drinks.history: Charles H. Baker Jr. wrote it into his 1946 book The Gentleman's Companion, naming it for the USS Maine, whose sinking in Havana harbour in 1898 helped trigger the Spanish-American War. Rye, sweet vermouth, cherry brandy and a rinse of absinthe.
steps: Stir rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, cherry liqueur and a few drops of absinthe with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Created by writer Charles H. Baker, named for the battleship whose sinking helped spark the Spanish–American War.

drinks.title: Retour Chez Moi Ti'Punch
drinks.author: Ashera Goonewardene
steps: Rub grapefruit zest around inside of serving glass.

Squeeze grapefruit juice by hand directly into stirring glass. Add Clément Canne Bleue, Lychi liqueur, Sirop, and Guava juice. Swizzle to mix and fine strain (to remove pulp) into serving glass (no ice). Ensure all liquid ingredients are pre-chilled to achieve a cold Ti'Punch without the need for ice, avoiding unwanted dilution.
Garnish with grapefruit zest twist.

drinks.title: Reversed Vesper & Tonic 'Martini
steps: This cocktail is inspired by Kate Moss's drink of choice—a vodka and tonic—elevated with the sophisticated ingredients of a Vesper and the addition of tonic water.
Combine gin, vodka, dry vermouth, and tonic water in a cocktail shaker filled with ice. Stir well until chilled, 15 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and serve immediately.

drinks.title: Rob Roy
drinks.history: Made at the Waldorf Astoria bar and named for an operetta about the Scottish outlaw Rob Roy MacGregor that had just opened on Broadway. It is a Manhattan with scotch.
steps: Stir scotch whisky, sweet vermouth and angostura bitters with plenty of ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a maraschino cherry.
-- Essentially a Manhattan made with Scotch instead of rye — named after the operetta "Rob Roy", playing on Broadway when it was invented.

drinks.title: Roosevelt Martini
steps: This classic martini honors Franklin D. Roosevelt, the 32nd U.S. President who repealed Prohibition. Combine gin and dry vermouth in a cocktail shaker with ice and stir until well chilled, 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with olive or a lemon twist.

drinks.title: Rum Old Fashioned
drinks.history: The 1806 cocktail template — spirit, sugar, bitters — moved onto aged rum. Re-basing the classics onto other spirits is one of the craft revival's standing habits, and this is among the few that stuck.
steps: Stir dark rum, sugar syrup and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange twist.

drinks.title: Rum Punch
steps: Mix rum, lime juice, sugar syrup, and spice together. Top with water and ice, stirring well to combine.

Note: This recipe follows the classic punch proportions of "one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong and four of weak" — adjust quantities based on your preferred punch bowl size and serving numbers. The "strong" refers to overproof rum, the "sour" to lime juice, the "sweet" to sugar syrup, and the "weak" to water.

drinks.title: Rum Swizzle
drinks.history: Whipped with a swizzle stick — traditionally a forked branch from the swizzle-stick tree, rolled between the palms until it froths — rather than shaken or stirred. The Swizzle Inn in Bermuda has served its own version since 1932.
steps: Fill a glass with crushed ice.
Add dark rum, orange juice, pineapple juice, lime juice and a dash of angostura bitters.
Swizzle briskly with a stirring stick until the glass frosts over.
-- Bermuda's national drink, traditionally mixed by spinning a swizzle stick between the palms.

drinks.title: Rusty Nail
drinks.history: Scotch and Drambuie had been mixed under half a dozen names since the 1930s; the Rusty Nail label settled in the early 1960s, when it became a Rat Pack drink.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Add scotch whisky and drambuie, then stir gently.
-- Named for the tool supposedly used to stir the first one — Drambuie is a Scotch-based honey and herb liqueur.

drinks.title: Sabot
steps: Mix gin, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and top with champagne.

drinks.title: Salty Dog
drinks.history: It began as gin and grapefruit; the salted rim and the switch to vodka came later. A salty dog was slang for an old sailor, one perpetually soaked in spray.
steps: Rim a rocks glass with salt and fill with ice.
Add vodka and top with grapefruit juice.
-- Without the salt rim, the same drink is called a Greyhound.

drinks.title: Sambuca Shot
drinks.history: An anise liqueur from the port near Rome. Served con la mosca — with the fly — meaning three coffee beans, for health, happiness and prosperity. Setting it alight is a bar-trade habit, not an Italian one.
steps: Pour sambuca into a shot glass. Garnish with three coffee beans.

drinks.title: Sangria
drinks.history: Descended from an old Iberian tradition of stretching and sweetening wine with fruit and spirit, going back centuries as an everyday drink rather than a cocktail-bar invention — it reached a much wider international audience after being served at the Spain Pavilion at the 1964 New York World's Fair.
steps: In a large jug, combine red wine, brandy, orange liqueur and sugar syrup. Add orange, apple and lemon, all sliced, and stir. Chill for at least an hour, then serve over ice in wine glasses, topped with a splash of soda water per glass.
notes: The longer it sits before serving, the better — a few hours or overnight lets the fruit properly flavour the wine rather than just floating in it.

drinks.title: Sangria (Sangaree)
steps: This traditional Spanish sangria celebrates La Rioja's famous wine region. The exact ingredient proportions were not provided in the source material, so this represents a standard sangria preparation. Mix red wine with brandy, orange juice, lemon juice, and sugar in a large pitcher. Add sliced orange, lemon, and apple. Stir well and let chill for at least 2 hours before serving over ice in wine glasses.

drinks.title: Saturn
drinks.history: Won the International Bartenders Association world championship for J. "Popo" Galsini. It is one of very few tiki drinks built on gin rather than rum, and was lost for decades before the tiki revival dug it out.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice, passion fruit syrup, orgeat and falernum hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Sazerac
drinks.history: It began as cognac dosed with the apothecary Antoine Peychaud's own bitters. The base moved to rye after phylloxera destroyed the French vineyards in the 1870s, and the absinthe rinse joined later still. It was named the official cocktail of New Orleans in 2008.
steps: Chill a rocks glass, then swirl a dash of absinthe around it to coat and discard the excess.
Muddle a sugar cube with peychaud's bitters and angostura bitters in a separate glass, then add rye whiskey and stir with ice until well chilled.
Strain into the prepared glass — no ice — and garnish with a twist of lemon peel.
-- Widely considered America's oldest known cocktail, dating back to 1830s New Orleans.

drinks.title: Scofflaw
drinks.history: Scofflaw" was the winning entry in a real 1923 Boston newspaper competition to coin a word for someone who openly flouted Prohibition — Harry's New York Bar in Paris promptly named a cocktail after it, using smuggled rye rather than gin as a nod to the word's American origins.
steps: Shake rye whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice, grenadine and orange bitters hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.
notes: A genuinely rare thing: a cocktail named after a word invented specifically for a competition, rather than the other way round.

drinks.title: Scooby Snack
drinks.history: Melon liqueur, coconut rum, pineapple and cream, named after the cartoon dog's biscuits. Usually shaken rather than layered, which makes it a small milkshake.
steps: Shake melon liqueur, coconut rum, pineapple juice and cream briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Scorpion
drinks.history: A Trader Vic's punch, traditionally served in a communal bowl with long straws and a gardenia floating in the middle.
steps: Blend white rum, brandy, orange juice, lemon juice and orgeat with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth, then pour into a Hurricane glass.

drinks.title: Scorpion Bowl
drinks.history: A Trader Vic's punch, traditionally served in a communal bowl with long straws and a gardenia floating in the middle.
steps: Shake white rum, brandy, orange juice, lemon juice and orgeat hard with ice.
Strain into a large glass or bowl over crushed ice, and garnish with a sprig of mint.
-- A tiki-bar sharing drink, traditionally served with two long straws.

drinks.title: Screaming Orgasm
drinks.history: The Orgasm — amaretto, coffee liqueur and Irish cream — with vodka added, which is the screaming part. The naming logic of the decade in a single glass.
steps: Shake vodka, coffee liqueur, irish cream and amaretto briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Screwdriver
drinks.author: Difford's
steps: Pour vodka into a glass filled with ice. Top with fresh orange juice, freshly squeezed from ripe oranges.
Add a dash of sugar and a dash of orange bitters to bring out the flavors. Stir well with a clean screwdriver (or bar spoon).

drinks.title: Sea Breeze
drinks.history: The original Sea Breeze was gin and apricot brandy. The vodka, cranberry and grapefruit version belongs to the 1960s and 70s, when Ocean Spray was pushing cranberry juice hard into American bars.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add vodka, cranberry juice and grapefruit juice.
Stir gently and garnish with a lime wedge.
-- A 1980s update of the older Cape Codder, with grapefruit juice added.

drinks.title: Sex on the Beach
drinks.history: Created at Confetti's during spring break, when a peach schnapps distributor ran a sales contest and a bartender needed a name that would sell it to students. It worked.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add vodka, peach schnapps, orange juice and cranberry juice, then stir well.
Garnish with a slice of orange and a maraschino cherry.
-- A 1980s Florida bar-promotion drink that became one of the best-known fruity cocktails of all time.

drinks.title: Sgroppino
drinks.history: Lemon sorbet whipped with prosecco and vodka, served between courses or at the end of a long meal. The name comes from the Venetian for untying — what it is meant to do to a knotted stomach.
steps: Whisk lemon sorbet with vodka in a chilled bowl until smooth and slushy.
Pour into a chilled glass and slowly top with prosecco, stirring gently to combine. No ice.

drinks.title: Sherry Cobbler
drinks.history: The drink that popularised the drinking straw and drove enormous demand for ice. Dickens gave it a rapturous page in Martin Chuzzlewit in 1844, and it was the most popular drink in America for a good part of the century.
steps: Fill a wine glass with crushed ice and add sherry and sugar syrup.
Stir and garnish generously with orange and seasonal fruit, plus a mint sprig.
-- A 19th-century American sensation credited with popularising both crushed ice and the drinking straw.

drinks.title: Sichuan Pepper + Sesame Oil Fat-Washed Cocktail Recipes
drinks.glass: Martini glass / Highball glass / Rocks glass
drinks.author: Kathy Yuan
steps: ## Fat-Washing (at least 1 day prior)

Combine gin with tengjiaoyou (green Sichuan pepper oil) in one resealable jar and whiskey with toasted sesame oil in another. Seal and shake vigorously to combine, once per hour for 2-3 hours. Chill in freezer overnight (or at least 6-8 hours) to separate and solidify the oils.
