The next day, when the oil has solidified, prepare cheesecloth over a strainer or chinois. Strain out the solids and store the fat-washed liquor in a cool, dark place.
## Sichuan Pepper Martini ft. Tengjiaoyou

Combine fat-washed gin and dry vermouth in a cocktail shaker or mixing glass. Fill with ice and stir for at least 30 seconds, until the aromas have bloomed to your liking. Strain into a chilled martini glass. Garnish with a lemon peel and/or olive, as desired. If using lemon, twist it over the poured drink to express the oil content in the peel.
## Sichuan Pepper Gin Fizz ft. Tengjiaoyou

Combine fat-washed gin, lemon juice (freshly squeezed){22%ml}, simple syrup, and egg white in a cocktail shaker. Dry-shake vigorously for about 15 seconds to ensure a foamy egg white. Fill shaker with ice, then shake another 30 seconds or until chilled. Strain into a chilled tall glass and top with club soda. Garnish with lemon peel as desired.
## Manhattan ft. Toasted Sesame Oil

Combine fat-washed whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters in a cocktail shaker or mixing glass. Fill with ice and stir for 20-30 seconds, until chilled. Strain into a chilled rocks glass with or without ice. Garnish with lemon peel or Luxardo cherry as desired.

drinks.title: Sidecar
drinks.history: Both the Ritz in Paris and Buck's Club in London claim it. The name is said to come from an army captain who arrived at the bar in a motorcycle sidecar. It appears in print twice in 1922, in books by Harry MacElhone and Robert Vermeire.
steps: Rub a wedge of lemon around the rim of a chilled coupe glass and dip in caster sugar to coat, if you like.
Shake cognac, triple sec and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into the glass.
-- Said to have been invented in a Paris bar for a customer who arrived by motorcycle sidecar — one of the first "sour" cocktails to use a whole citrus measure.

drinks.title: Silk Panties
drinks.history: Vodka and peach schnapps, nothing else. Peach schnapps carried an extraordinary number of drinks through those two decades, and this is the shortest of them.
steps: Shake vodka and peach schnapps briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Simple Banana Tea
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour water into a saucepan and heat until simmering.
Wash organic banana in warm water, cut both ends off and split the banana lengthways.
Place banana halves with the skin still on into the boiling water and simmer 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and leave the banana to steep in the hot water 10 minutes.
Strain and pour the banana tea directly into cups to serve, or into a sealed container to store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days for use as a cocktail ingredient.

drinks.title: Singapore Sling
drinks.author: Dale DeGroff
steps: Pour dry gin, cherry brandy liqueur, triple sec, and Bénédictine into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Add fresh pineapple juice and citrus juice (lemon or lime).
Add a dash of grenadine and a couple of dashes of bitters.
Shake well and strain into a highball glass filled with ice.
Top with a splash of soda water if desired. Serve with a pineapple wedge and cherry garnish.

drinks.title: Single Speed Spritz
drinks.author: Merlin Griffiths
steps: Build Martini Bianco, lemon juice, elderflower cordial and a dash of orange bitters with cubed ice in a cooler glass, then stir 30 seconds.
Top with soda water and garnish with a large grapefruit twist.

drinks.title: Sisterhood Cocktail
drinks.author: Lauren Mote
steps: Shake Zacapa 23 rum, Cherry Heering, lemon juice, cinnamon syrup, and Bittered Sling Malagasy Chocolate Bitters with ice and fine strain into cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lemon zest twist.

drinks.title: Skittle Bomb
drinks.history: Cointreau dropped into Red Bull, which together taste uncannily like the sweet. A British student bar invention of the energy-drink era.
steps: Pour cointreau into a shot glass.
Drop it into a glass of energy drink and drink straight away.

drinks.title: Slippery Nipple
drinks.history: Sambuca with a layer of Irish cream. One of a whole generation of shots whose names were the marketing, and whose creators are entirely unrecorded.
steps: Slowly layer sambuca and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Sloe Gin
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pick ripe sloe berries from the blackthorn bush. (Alternatively, buy freshly picked berries online.)
Wash berries in a colander under running water and discard any that look bruised or burst.
Freeze berries for at least 24 hours to open fruit cells and allow better infusion in alcohol.
Place frozen sloe berries in a sterilised sealable bottling jar (such as a Kilner jar with 1.5 litre capacity).
Cover berries with gin, Navy strength (at least 47% alcohol, such as Tanqueray). — Use a decent quality gin
Seal jar and shake vigorously.
Leave to infuse in a dark place at room temperature for at least 2 months, shaking every few days.

Strain through a fine sieve and muslin into a large sterile mixing bowl. (You'll be left mostly with stones and skins; some people crush the stones and return them to steep further to extract almond notes, or add crushed almonds at the start instead.)
Gradually add and stir in sugar syrup made from water and caster sugar, adjusting to taste. You may also adjust the strength and concentration by adding more gin and/or distilled water at this stage.
Bottle and leave to mature for between 1 month and 7 years before drinking. This is traditionally a Christmas tipple, best laid down and kept until at least the following Christmas.

drinks.title: Sloe Gin Fizz
drinks.history: The Gin Fizz template with sloe gin — an English hedgerow liqueur, made by steeping the sour fruit of the blackthorn — in place of the dry gin, which sweetens and reddens the whole drink.
steps: Shake sloe gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a highball glass over ice and top with soda water.
-- Sloe gin isn't really gin at all — it's a liqueur made by steeping sloe berries in gin.

drinks.title: Sloppy Joe
steps: This cocktail celebrates National Sloppy Joe Day with a spirit-forward drink that's far less messy than its sandwich namesake, yet just as delicious.
Mix bourbon, sloe gin, and fresh lemon juice together in a cocktail shaker with ice. Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish as desired and serve immediately.

drinks.title: Slow Negroni
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour gin, sloe gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth into a mixing glass filled with ice. Stir well until chilled, then strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice. Serve as a classic Negroni with sloe berry flavour notes.

drinks.title: Slow Screw Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour sloe gin and dry gin into a glass filled with ice.
Top with freshly squeezed orange juice and stir gently to combine.
Serve immediately.

drinks.title: Smoke & Mirrors
steps: Pour Glenmorangie Quinta Ruban into a rocks glass over ice. Add Hojisha tea wood smoke and blackberry and raspberry shrub. Finish with Antica Formula sweet vermouth and stir gently to combine.

drinks.title: Smoked Pineapple Ginger Collins With Chipotle Salt Rim
drinks.author: David Robinson

ingredients.name: smoked pineapple and ginger tepache reduction

steps: Rim a collins glass with chipotle salt for the rim and set aside.
In a shaker, combine Patrón Reposado, Patrón Citronage, smoked pineapple and ginger tepache reduction, freshly squeezed lime juice, and vermouth with ice.
Shake until chilled and combined, then strain into the rimmed glass.

drinks.title: Smoked Salty Sour
steps: Add Scotch whisky, influenced by salty Islay peaty malt, Green Chartreuse, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice to a shaker with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with a smoking cinnamon stick or smoked salt rim to complement the Islay peaty character.

drinks.title: Smokestack Mary
steps: Pour gin into a glass filled with ice. Add tomato juice, chipotle, smoked paprika, and peated Scotch. Stir well to combine.
Top with ice if needed and serve immediately.

drinks.title: Snakebite
drinks.history: A staple of UK pub culture — lager and cider mixed half and half — that picked up a slightly dangerous reputation in the 1980s and 90s, with some pubs at the time refusing to serve it or to sell it topped with blackcurrant cordial (a "snakebite and black"), on the belief it caused unusually bad hangovers or aggressive drunkenness. There is no real chemical basis for the reputation.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add lager and cider and stir briefly.
notes: Equal parts lager and cider, poured together in one glass — the "and black" version adds a dash of blackcurrant cordial on top.

drinks.title: Snowball
drinks.history: Advocaat with lemonade and a squeeze of lime — a fixture of the British Christmas drinks trolley, and for many households the only cocktail of the year. Advocaat itself is Dutch, made from eggs, sugar and brandy.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add advocaat and lime cordial and stir briefly. Top with lemonade.

drinks.title: Sombrero
drinks.history: Coffee liqueur poured over cream or milk, named for the layered look in the glass. A quieter, milkier relative of the Black Russian and White Russian from the same coffee-liqueur boom.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add coffee liqueur.
Float cream on top.
-- About as simple as after-dinner drinks get — just two ingredients over ice.

drinks.title: Sour Apple Shot
drinks.history: Apple schnapps and vodka. Sour apple was the defining flavour of late-1990s bars, and this was its plainest expression.
steps: Shake vodka, apple schnapps and lime juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Southside
drinks.history: The 21 Club in New York claims it. So does Chicago, where the story goes that the South Side gangs got the rougher gin and needed mint and lemon to make it drinkable. It is essentially a Mojito made with gin.
steps: Shake gin, lime juice, sugar syrup and mint leaves hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Essentially a gin Mojito without the soda — a favourite of Al Capone's crew, by one story.

drinks.title: Springbok
drinks.history: Amarula and crème de menthe layered green over gold, after the national rugby team's colours. Amarula is made from the fruit of the marula tree, which elephants are famously fond of.
steps: Slowly layer crème de menthe and amarula into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Stinger
drinks.history: A high-society digestif — brandy and white crème de menthe, nothing else. Reginald Vanderbilt is usually credited. It appears throughout interwar fiction as the drink of people who own boats.
steps: Shake cognac and white crème de menthe hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- A minty after-dinner favourite from the early 1900s that fell out of fashion but never quite disappeared.

drinks.title: Stone Sour
steps: Add bourbon, apricot liqueur, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice.
Garnish with an apricot slice or twist if desired.

drinks.title: Storehouse Martini
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "rich, bold, creamy" — an espresso martini built on vanilla vodka and Kahlúa, deepened with a Guinness and demerara sugar reduction in place of a plain sugar syrup. The name nods to the stout. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka, Kahlúa, cooled espresso and Guinness and demerara reduction hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker for a good foam, then strain into a chilled martini glass. Garnish with three coffee beans.
notes: Rich, bold and creamy, per the bar's own menu — a stout-and-coffee twist on the espresso martini rather than a straight copy of it.
The Guinness and demerara reduction is simmered stout reduced down with demerara sugar until syrupy; make a batch and it keeps in the fridge for other coffee drinks too.

drinks.title: Strawberry Daiquiri
drinks.history: El Floridita added fresh fruit to the frozen daiquiri once the blender arrived in the 1930s; strawberry became the standard flavour once American frozen-drink machines put it on every beach bar menu decades later.
steps: Blend white rum, strawberries, lime juice and sugar syrup with a scoop of crushed ice until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass.
-- The most popular of the frozen Daiquiris, made the same way as the banana version with strawberries in place of banana.

drinks.title: Strawberry Soul Hard Shake
drinks.author: Jane Ryan
steps: Combine Bailey's Irish Cream, strawberry ice cream, cream, and marshmallows in a blender.
Blend until smooth 1 minute, then pour into a chilled glass and serve immediately.

drinks.title: Suave Agave Cocktail
drinks.author: Andy Seymour
steps: Combine tequila Don Julio Reposado, Malbec wine, pomegranate juice and simple syrup into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake vigorously and strain into a wine glass.
Garnish with an orange wheel.

drinks.title: Surfer on Acid
drinks.history: Jägermeister with coconut rum and pineapple — the combination that convinced a generation Jägermeister could taste tropical.
steps: Shake jägermeister, coconut rum and pineapple juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Swamp Juice
steps: Put the leaves of the fresh mint into a pestle and mortar with a pinch of white sugar and bruise it down (don't liquidise). Rinse the pestle and mortar out with a bit of vodka into a large bowl.
Add all the lime juice (juiced) and pulp into the bowl too, along with the rest of the vodka, the white rum, and the runny honey.
Stir it up so the honey gets mixed in and allow it to marinade in the fridge for a day if possible, or minutes if you can't.
Take a large highball glass (holding at least 425 ml), fill it with whole and half-crushed ice, then half fill with the boozy mixture and top off with ginger beer.
Drink. Share. Fall over. Repeat.

-- Full name is Dr Lucy Darawallahs Swamp Fever, named after a doctor in Nairobi who inspired the vodka honey bit, a character in a John Irving novel (misspelled), and an 11 yr old niece who introduced some of the chaos that resulted in the elixir itself. — For sweetness, start off with slightly less honey the first time and see if that's sweet enough; you can always add more later. If you hate ginger beer, try tonic instead.

drinks.title: Swedish Punsch (Arrack Punsch)
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Mix Batavia arrack with white rum (or vodka as alternative). Add sugar syrup to sweeten. Flavor with lemon zest and nutmeg, grating fresh nutmeg if possible. Stir well to combine.
Optional: add cardamom and cinnamon for additional spice complexity. Serve cold as a liqueur, particularly as a digestive with coffee.

drinks.title: Tangy Feeling
drinks.author: Fabio Immovilli
steps: MUDDLE basil and white grapes in base of shaker. Add Cîroc Vodka, apple shrub, apple juice, lemon curd and grapefruit bitters. SHAKE with ice and strain into silver mug filled with crushed ice.
Garnish with grapes, basil and lemon.

drinks.title: Tequila Slammer
drinks.history: Tequila with lemonade, covered with the hand, slammed on the bar to make it froth and drunk in one while it is still fizzing.
steps: Pour tequila and lemon-lime soda into a rocks glass.
Cover with your hand, slam it once on the bar to make it fizz, and drink it in one while it's still foaming.
-- A party-shot classic that spread through nightclubs worldwide in the 1980s.

drinks.title: Tequila Sunrise
drinks.history: Bobby Lozoff and Billy Rice made it at the Trident. The Rolling Stones drank it there before their 1972 American tour and named the tour after it. An earlier 1930s Arizona drink of the same name used crème de cassis and looked nothing like it.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add tequila and orange juice.
Slowly pour grenadine down the inside of the glass so it sinks and settles at the bottom.
Do not stir — garnish with a slice of orange and a maraschino cherry.
-- The layered "sunrise" effect comes from the grenadine's density, which pulls it below the lighter orange juice.

drinks.title: Tequila Sunrise Cocktail
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice cubes.
Pour tequila blanco and orange juice into the glass and stir.
Slowly pour grenadine into the glass to create the sunrise color effect — it has to be slow!
Garnish with orange wedge and maraschino cherry.
The cocktail is now ready to enjoy.

drinks.title: Test Tube Baby
drinks.history: Said to be named after the birth of Louise Brown in 1978, the first baby conceived by IVF, and served in an actual test tube wherever a bar could find them.
steps: Slowly layer amaretto, coconut rum and irish cream into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: The 1693 Day Negroni
drinks.author: Denny Kallivoka, Eleni Nikoloulia
steps: Combine gin (a London dry gin blend: Greenall's, Martin Miller's, Fifty Pounds, or Gordon's), Campari, and Cocchi Americano in a mixing glass with ice.
Stir well for 30 seconds until properly chilled and diluted.
Strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice or ice.
Garnish with an orange peel expressed over the surface and dropped in as a twist.

-- Note: This recipe documents the classic fresh Negroni formula. Christos Chouseas's 1693-day aged version was an experimental aging project stored in a sealed glass container for 4.5 years. The aging process significantly altered the cocktail's character, reducing gin prominence and creating a more fortified, sherry-like spirit. This version is best enjoyed as a digestif.

drinks.title: The Addington
drinks.author: Guy Butler
steps: Stir Martell VS Cognac, Cocchi Vermouth di Torino, Benedictine DOM liqueur, and Bokers Bitters with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
Garnish with lemon.

drinks.title: The Aul Lammas Fair
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "sweet, citrus, balanced" and named for Ballycastle's Auld Lammas Fair — Ireland's oldest traditional fair, held every August since the 17th century, famous above all for yellowman, the hard golden honeycomb toffee sold from its stalls (as the old ballad goes: "Did you treat your Mary Ann / to some Dulse and Yellow Man / at the Ould Lammas Fair in Ballycastle-O"). The drink's nod to it is YellaMan, an actual honeycomb vodka liqueur made by Niche Drinks in nearby Derry/Londonderry, lengthened here with Cointreau, marmalade, lime and lemonade. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate — and since YellaMan is a liqueur rather than a plain vodka, it's already sweetened, so this needs less added sugar than a typical vodka sour.
steps: Shake YellaMan honeycomb vodka liqueur, Cointreau, marmalade and lime juice hard with ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a highball glass over fresh ice. Top with lemonade. Garnish with a lime wheel.
notes: Sweet, citrus and balanced, per the bar's own menu — the YellaMan liqueur is what makes this one, giving it a honeycomb sweetness no ordinary vodka sour has. If you can't get hold of it, a plain vodka with a splash of extra honey syrup is the closest substitute.

drinks.title: The Bloody Mary Cocktail
drinks.author: Simon Difford & Jack McGarry
steps: Cover the bottom of a cocktail shaker with salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, and a layer of Worcestershire sauce. Add lemon juice and ice.
Pour vodka and tomato juice (thick tomato juice preferred) into the shaker. Shake vigorously 10 seconds, then strain and pour into a highball glass.
Serve cold and garnish with a celery stick if desired.

drinks.title: The British Raj Cocktail
drinks.author: Ashish Sharma

ingredients.name: Old Monk rum infused with cinnamon, clove and coriander
Martini Rosso infused with gunpowder spices

steps: Stir Old Monk rum infused with cinnamon, clove and coriander, Cherry Heering, Averna Amaro, Martini Rosso infused with gunpowder spices, Earl Grey tea tincture, and Angostura Aromatic Bitters with ice and strain into a chilled Martini glass.
Garnish with orange zest twist and cinnamon stick.

drinks.title: The Empire of Dreams
drinks.author: Fred Siggins
steps: Shake rum, pineapple juice, apricot brandy, lime juice, orgeat syrup and espresso beans with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
Garnish with a twist of lime peel.

drinks.title: The Endless Journey
drinks.author: Greg Almeida
steps: Throw Patrón Reposado, mole distillate, Suze Gentiane bitter, and jasmine and almond horchata with ice and strain into a wooden cup.
Dust the top with freshly grated nutmeg to garnish.

drinks.title: The Hackney Handshake
drinks.author: Brandon Phillips
steps: Shake beefeater gin, Lustau Manzanilla sherry, lemon juice, and Movie Night Syrup with egg white and ice 10 seconds.
Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Garnish with juniper dusted popcorn.

drinks.title: The Jimmy Bedford
drinks.author: Kelley Slagle
steps: For the Pickled Apple Syrup, combine apple juice, apple cider vinegar and sugar. Reduce over a very low heat to 50 per cent of original volume. This takes approximately 90 minutes. Chill before using.
Prepare the apple slice garnish by pickling it in equal parts apple cider vinegar and water.
Shake Jack Daniels and Pickled Apple Syrup with ice and strain over a single very large ice cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with the pickled apple slice.

drinks.title: The Knight Cup
drinks.author: Elizaveta Evdokimova
steps: Stir Bacardi Superior rum, artichoke liqueur, grenadine liqueur, and sugar syrup with ice and strain into an ice-filled old fashioned glass.
Garnish with pomegranate leather.

drinks.title: The Sloe Sling
drinks.author: Nick Kobbernagel Hovind
steps: SHAKE cherry heering, sloe gin, Aalborg Taffel Aquavit, Peychaud's bitters, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass 1 minutes.
TOP with soda water and garnish with a mint sprig.

drinks.title: The Sweet Talker
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nostalgic, sweet" — bon-bon-infused vodka lengthened with blood orange tonic, built long over ice. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice, add bon-bon-infused vodka, lemon juice and sugar and stir briefly. Top with blood orange tonic. Garnish with a lemon wheel.
notes: Nostalgic and sweet, per the bar's own menu — built for anyone who wants their vodka to taste like a sweet shop.

drinks.title: Three Cents Paloma
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour tequila blanco into a glass filled with ice.
Add lime juice with a squeeze.
Top up with Three Cents Grapefruit Soda.
Stir gently and serve.

drinks.title: Three Wise Men
drinks.history: Jack Daniel's, Jim Beam and Johnnie Walker in one glass — three men, hence the joke. Adding José Cuervo makes it the Four Horsemen.
steps: Pour bourbon, scotch whisky and tennessee whiskey into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Ti' Punch
steps: Pour rhum agricole into a glass filled with ice cubes.
Add lime squeezed and cane syrup.
Stir gently and serve.

drinks.title: Toffee Apple Shot
drinks.history: Toffee vodka with apple juice — a bonfire-night flavour, and a fixture of British bars every autumn since flavoured vodkas took hold.
steps: Shake apple schnapps and butterscotch schnapps briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Tokyo Iced Tea
drinks.history: The Long Island template with Midori, which turns it bright green. Nothing about it is Japanese except the melon liqueur.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add vodka, gin, white rum, tequila, triple sec, melon liqueur and lemon juice and stir briefly. Top with lemonade.

drinks.title: Told You So
drinks.author: Dinos Constantinides
steps: Shake Cherry Heering, London dry gin, Vermouth Mancino Secco, fresh plum juice, beetroot oleo-saccharum, salt, and black pepper with ice and fine strain into a chilled coupe glass. Top with Champagne.
Garnish with a chunk of block ice.
For the beetroot oleo-saccharum: slice steamed beetroot and place in a vacuum-pack bag with caster sugar, peels of lime, and seal. Cook sous vide 2 hours at 60°C. Strain through a Superbag.

drinks.title: Tom Collins
drinks.history: Jerry Thomas printed the recipe in 1876, but the name comes from the Great Tom Collins Hoax of 1874, when New Yorkers amused themselves by telling friends that a man named Tom Collins was in a bar down the road slandering them. The victim would storm in demanding Tom Collins, and be handed a drink.
steps: Shake gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup with ice.
Strain into a collins glass over ice and top with soda water.
-- A "John Collins" swaps the gin for whiskey.

drinks.title: Tomatini
drinks.author: Jimmy Barrat
steps: Add vodka, fresh tomato juice, and white balsamic vinegar to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake vigorously 10 seconds and strain into a chilled martini glass.
Garnish with a fresh bull's heart tomato slice or cherry tomato on a pick.

drinks.title: Tommy's Margarita
drinks.history: Julio Bermejo, at his family's restaurant Tommy's, replaced the triple sec with agave nectar so the tequila would taste of itself. It is now the version most serious bars pour, and Bermejo has spent thirty years teaching Americans about 100% agave tequila.
steps: Shake tequila, lime juice and agave syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice, salt rim optional.
-- Created at Tommy's in San Francisco, replacing the classic Margarita's triple sec with agave nectar.

drinks.title: Toronto
drinks.history: Robert Vermeire printed it in 1922 as the Fernet Cocktail, noting that it was a favourite around Toronto. Canadian whisky with a bracing dose of Fernet-Branca.
steps: Stir rye whiskey, fernet, sugar syrup and angostura bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Rocks glass over fresh ice.

drinks.title: Trade and Navigation Cocktail with Cherry Heering
drinks.author: Nick Kobbernagel Hovind
steps: Stir Cherry Heering, Batavia Arrack, and Aalborg Taffel Aquavit with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
Garnish with star anise.

drinks.title: Traffic Light
drinks.history: Three layers of red, yellow and green liqueur — usually grenadine, banana or Galliano, and melon. The colours are the recipe; the taste is incidental.
steps: Slowly layer melon liqueur, galliano and sloe gin into a shot glass in the order listed, pouring each over the back of a bar spoon so they settle in bands.

drinks.title: Trinidad Sour
drinks.history: Giuseppe González created it at Clover Club — a sour built on an entire measure and a half of Angostura bitters as the base spirit, which was unheard of at the time. It became one of the most influential drinks of the 2010s cocktail scene.
steps: Shake angostura bitters, orgeat, lemon juice and rye whiskey hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- An unusual modern classic that flips the usual ratio, using bitters as the base spirit rather than a seasoning.

drinks.title: Turmeric Milk Recipe (Haldi Doodh)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: Bring milk to a gentle boil in a pot.

Turn off the heat and allow the milk to cool down to a slightly hot temperature. Add turmeric powder (or use 2 pinches to 1/4 teaspoon for kids) and black pepper ground (or long pepper powder). Mix well until the turmeric blends completely with the milk.

Transfer the turmeric milk to a cup and consume while still warm. You may strain the milk if preferred. Add sweetener like sugar, jaggery, or honey if desired, but only add honey once the milk has cooled to warm temperature.

-- Optional spices for flavor: add ground cardamom, ground cinnamon, ground ginger, or clove (crushed) to the milk while boiling for 2 minutes before turning off heat. Traditional ayurvedic turmeric milk uses only milk, turmeric and black pepper without sweetener.

drinks.title: Turmeric Tea Recipe (Golden Tea with No-Brew Option)
drinks.author: Swasthi Shreekanth
steps: **Option 1 – No-Brew Method**

Add turmeric powder (or fresh turmeric root chopped if using fresh), dried ground ginger, ground black pepper, ghee or cold pressed oil (such as avocado, olive, or coconut oil), and lemon juice to a cup. Bring water to a rolling boil in a kettle or pot and pour into the cup.
Stir well and cover. Let steep for 2 minutes and serve. If desired, add a sweetener like honey or jaggery.
**Option 2 – Saucepan Method**
Mix together water, turmeric powder (or fresh turmeric root chopped), ginger chopped (or dried ground ginger), and ground black pepper (or whole black peppercorns crushed) in a small pot or pan.
Bring to a boil and reduce the heat to medium. Simmer for 4-8 minutes, depending on how strong you want the drink to be. — Ground turmeric requires 4 mins; chopped turmeric requires about 8 mins.
Stir in ghee or oil and strain into a cup. You may stir in honey if you prefer, but only add to warm tea (not hot).
If desired, stir in lemon juice or warm orange juice. If the tea is too strong for your taste, simply add more hot water (not cold) to dilute.

**Optional Spices** (for enhanced digestive and respiratory benefits): Coarsely crush cardamom, clove, true cinnamon, cumin seeds, carom seeds, and fennel seeds using a mortar and pestle. Add to the pot and boil for 10 minutes instead of the standard time.

drinks.title: Tuxedo
drinks.history: Named for the Tuxedo Club in Tuxedo Park, New York — the same club that gave the dinner jacket its American name after a member wore a tailless one to the autumn ball.
steps: Stir gin, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur, absinthe and orange bitters with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Coupe glass.

drinks.title: Twentieth Century
drinks.history: Named after the 20th Century Limited, the famously glamorous express train that ran between New York and Chicago, and credited to bartender C. A. Tuck in W. J. Tarling's Café Royal Cocktail Book of 1937, the same decade the train was at its most fashionable.
steps: Shake gin, Lillet Blanc, crème de cacao and lemon juice hard with ice, then strain into a Coupe glass.
notes: White crème de cacao here, not dark — it should stay pale, not turn the drink brown.

drinks.title: Twinkle
drinks.history: Tony Conigliaro created it at Lonsdale House in Notting Hill. Vodka, elderflower and sparkling wine — one of the drinks that put elderflower into every British bar for the following decade.
steps: Stir vodka and elderflower liqueur with ice until well chilled, then strain into a Champagne flute. Top with champagne. Garnish with a lemon twist.

drinks.title: Untouchable Stone Sherry Cobbler
drinks.author: Lucia Montanelli
steps: Muddle pineapple and dried pineapple in the base of a shaker.
Add sherry, falernum, orgeat syrup, lime juice, and bitters.
Shake with ice and strain into a goblet filled with crushed ice.
Garnish with dried pineapple and fruit dusted with icing sugar.

drinks.title: Vampiro
drinks.history: Tequila with a savoury tomato-and-citrus mix closer to a Bloody Mary than a Margarita — sangrita's ingredients built straight into the glass rather than served alongside. Guadalajara's La Fuente cantina is often credited.
steps: Shake tequila, tomato juice, orange juice, lime juice and a dash of hot sauce hard with ice.
Strain into a glass over fresh ice.
-- A savoury Mexican cousin of the Bloody Mary, built on tequila instead of vodka.

drinks.title: Vanilla Flavoured Vodka
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Take vanilla pod and split lengthways with a sharp knife on a cutting board. Place the split pod in a freshly opened bottle of vodka and leave to infuse for 3 to 6 days, shaking occasionally 3-6 days. — Place the bottle somewhere you walk past regularly and shake each time you pass to increase extraction rate

After a week, pour the contents of the bottle into a clean container. Clean the bottle and then filter your now vanilla-flavoured vodka back into the bottle. Be sure to mark the bottle "vanilla-infused" to save confusion.

drinks.title: Vegas Bomb
drinks.history: Crown Royal and peach schnapps dropped into an energy drink. One of dozens of bombs that followed the Jägerbomb, and one of the few whose name stuck.
steps: Shake whisky, peach schnapps and cranberry juice with ice and strain into a shot glass.
Drop into a glass of energy drink and drink straight away.

drinks.title: Velvet Hammer
drinks.author: Luke Robinson

ingredients.name: Bepi Tosolini I Legni Rovere grappa

steps: STIR Bepi Tosolini I Legni Rovere grappa, Bepi Tosolini Amaro, Crème de fraise and Absinthe with ice and strain into chilled glass.
Garnish with mint and toasted coffee bean shells.

drinks.title: Venceremos
drinks.author: Chia-An (Gn) Chan
steps: MUDDLE pineapple leaves in base of shaker. Add Bacardi Carta Blanca, coconut liqueur, pineapple juice, cucumber juice, lime juice, and sesame oil. SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with ice.

drinks.title: Venetian Spritz
steps: Pour prosecco into a glass filled with ice.
Add aperol and soda water.
Stir gently and garnish with an orange slice.

drinks.title: Venetian Spritz (Spritz Al Bitter)
steps: Pour white wine into a wine glass filled with ice.
Add soda water to the glass.
Top with Aperol or other Italian bitter liqueur.
Stir gently to combine.
Garnish with an orange slice or lemon slice.

drinks.title: Vesper
drinks.history: Ian Fleming wrote it into Casino Royale and named it after Vesper Lynd. Kina Lillet, whose quinine bite balanced the drink, was reformulated in 1986 into today's much softer Lillet Blanc, so a modern Vesper does not taste like the one Bond ordered.
steps: Shake gin, vodka and lillet blanc hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with a lemon twist.
-- Named by Ian Fleming for the Bond girl in Casino Royale — "shaken, not stirred" is this drink's own instruction.

drinks.title: Vieux Carré
drinks.history: Walter Bergeron created it at the Carousel Bar in the Hotel Monteleone and named it for the Vieux Carré, the French Quarter. Rye and cognac together are what make it unmistakably New Orleans.
steps: Stir rye whiskey, cognac, sweet vermouth, bénédictine, peychaud's bitters and angostura bitters with plenty of ice until well chilled.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice and garnish with a twist of lemon peel.
-- Named after the French Quarter of New Orleans ("Old Square"), invented at the Hotel Monteleone in the 1930s.

drinks.title: Virgin Bramble
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a Bramble, built on Tanqueray 0.0% alcohol-free gin with grenadine and lime in place of the usual gin and crème de mûre. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with crushed ice, add Tanqueray 0.0%, lime juice and sugar syrup and stir briefly. Drizzle grenadine over the top of the crushed ice last, unstirred, so it bleeds down through the glass. Garnish with a blackberry and a lime wedge.
notes: The drizzle is what makes a Bramble a Bramble, alcohol-free or not — pour the grenadine over crushed ice last and leave it alone rather than stirring it in.

drinks.title: Virgin Pornstar Martini
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a Pornstar Martini, built on passionfruit purée, lime and sugar syrup lengthened with pineapple juice instead of vanilla vodka and Passoã. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake the pulp of passionfruit, lime juice, sugar syrup and pineapple juice hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with half a passionfruit balanced on the rim.
notes: Traditionally served with a shot of prosecco alongside — swap it for a splash of soda water or sparkling grape juice to keep this one fully alcohol-free.

drinks.title: Virgin Strawberry Daiquiri
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a frozen strawberry daiquiri, built on strawberries, lime, sugar syrup and grenadine with no rum. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Blend strawberries, lime juice, sugar syrup, grenadine and a scoop of ice until smooth, then pour into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a strawberry slit onto the rim.
notes: Blend it thick — the point of a frozen daiquiri, alcohol-free or not, is a proper slush rather than a thin smoothie.

drinks.title: Vodka Collins
drinks.history: The Tom/John Collins template rebased on vodka once it overtook gin as America's spirit through the 1950s and 60s — the same substitution that produced the Vodka Martini and Vodka Tonic.
steps: Shake vodka, lemon juice and sugar syrup with ice, then strain into a glass over fresh ice.
Top with soda water and garnish with a slice of lemon.
-- The vodka branch of the Collins family, alongside the gin-based Tom Collins and whiskey-based John Collins.

drinks.title: Vodka Cranberry Cocktail
drinks.history: Invented by Ocean Spray as the Red Devil to sell cranberry juice, and renamed the Cape Codder in the 1960s when the co-operative pushed it into bars.
drinks.author: A Couple Cooks
steps: Combine vodka with cranberry juice in a glass filled with ice.
Add maple syrup or simple syrup to sweeten the cocktail, adjusting to taste for a more vibrant color and less sugar content than traditional recipes.
Squeeze lime into the mixture and stir well to combine all ingredients.
Garnish with a lime wheel or cranberry if desired, and serve immediately over ice.

drinks.title: Vodka Espresso
drinks.author: Dick Bradsell
steps: Pour vodka into a shaker with espresso of freshly brewed strong coffee and sugar syrup. Add ice to the shaker and shake vigorously until well-chilled, 10 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and serve immediately. The drink should be topped with a thin layer of crema from the espresso.

drinks.title: Vodka Martini
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Pour vodka and dry vermouth into a mixing glass filled with ice. Stir well 30 seconds until well chilled and diluted. Strain into a chilled Martini glass.

drinks.title: Vodka Sour
drinks.history: The whiskey sour's template — spirit, citrus, sugar — rebased on vodka for the same reason every other classic got a vodka version once it became America's best-selling spirit.
steps: Shake vodka, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
-- Any base spirit can be swapped in for a "sour" — this is simply the vodka version.

drinks.title: Vodka Tonic
drinks.history: A Gin and Tonic with the gin taken out, arriving with the American vodka boom. What it loses in botanicals it gains in not tasting of anything, which was the point.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add vodka and top with tonic water.
Stir briefly and garnish with a wedge of lime.
-- About as simple as a mixed drink gets — vodka's cleaner cousin to the gin and tonic.

drinks.title: Vodkatini / Vodka Martini
steps: Stir vodka and dry vermouth with ice in a mixing glass for 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with olive or lemon twist.

drinks.title: Ward 8
drinks.history: Made at the Locke-Ober restaurant to celebrate the political boss Martin Lomasney's election win in Boston's eighth ward — the night before the votes were actually counted, which tells you something about how the ward was run.
steps: Shake rye whiskey, lemon juice, orange juice and grenadine hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
-- Named after a Boston political ward, reportedly to celebrate an election win in 1898.

drinks.title: Washington Apple
drinks.history: Canadian whisky with apple schnapps and cranberry, named after the apple-growing state rather than the capital.
steps: Shake whisky, apple schnapps and cranberry juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Watermelon Shot
drinks.history: Melon liqueur, vodka and cranberry, which together land close to watermelon. One of the run of fruit shooters that filled American bar menus in the decade.
steps: Shake vodka, melon liqueur and lemon juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Webster Martini
steps: Add gin, dry vermouth, and fruit juice to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well until chilled, then strain into a chilled coupe glass.
Serve with a citrus twist or cherry garnish.

drinks.title: Whiskey Mist
drinks.author: Chris Inglis
steps: Shake Monkey Shoulder, Cherry Marnier, Cocchi Torino, beetroot juice and chocolate bitters over ice and strain into an Ardbeg rinsed glass.

drinks.title: Whiskey Smash
drinks.history: Jerry Thomas printed a brandy smash in 1862 — spirit muddled with mint and citrus, a small julep in a rocks glass. Dale DeGroff's bourbon-and-lemon version at the Rainbow Room in the 1990s is what brought the format back.
steps: Muddle lemon wedges with mint leaves and sugar syrup in a shaker.
Add bourbon and ice, shake hard, then strain into a rocks glass over crushed ice.
Garnish with a mint sprig.
-- A modern update of the Whiskey Smash tradition, popularised by Dale DeGroff in the 2000s.

drinks.title: Whisky Highball
drinks.history: The highball crossed to Japan with Torii Shinjiro, founder of Suntory, who needed a way to sell domestic whisky to people who did not drink it neat. The haibōru is now the default way whisky is drunk there, and Suntory relaunched it to a new generation in the 2000s.
steps: Fill a Highball glass with ice, add whisky and stir briefly. Top with soda water. Garnish with a lemon twist.

drinks.title: Whisky Mac
drinks.history: Scotch whisky and green ginger wine, said to have been invented for British officers serving in India's hill stations, who found the ginger wine warmed a whisky enough for the cold evenings. A fixture of British pubs by the mid-20th century.
steps: Pour scotch whisky and ginger wine into a glass over ice and stir.
-- A no-fuss British classic for cold weather — equal parts scotch and ginger wine, traditionally served without ice at all.

drinks.title: White Lady
drinks.history: Harry MacElhone is said to have created the first White Lady at Ciro's in London in 1919, using brandy, crème de menthe and Cointreau. The gin version is disputed: the Savoy credits Harry Craddock, while Difford's suggests it may stem from Victor Cabrin and that Craddock popularised it in his 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.
steps: Shake gin, Cointreau and lemon juice hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Uses the Savoy Cocktail Book ratio of 2:1:1 (25 ml per part). MacElhone's later version is equal thirds; egg white is a modern, optional addition that is not in the early recipes.

drinks.title: White Moscato and Peach Sangria
drinks.author: Mely Martínez
steps: First, prepare the fruit by cutting peaches or nectarines in half, pole to pole around the pit, using the crease in the skin as a guide. Hold both halves of the fruit and twist apart. Once you remove the pit, slice into several wedges.
Place the fruit in a large pitcher. Add peach juice, orange liqueur, and white Moscato wine.
Stir well, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
To serve, fill glasses with ice cubes and add the sangria mixture dividing evenly. Top off each glass with club soda or sparkling water. — Use 591ml of club soda for all 8 servings or add to taste

drinks.title: White Negroni
drinks.author: Wayne Collins
steps: Stir gin, Suze and Lillet Blanc in an ice-filled glass.
Garnish with pink grapefruit zest.

drinks.title: White Noise
drinks.author: James Stevenson
steps: Add Diplomatico Blanco, Pedro Ximénez vermouth, Banana Rye Distillate, and Macadamia Syrup to a mixing glass, stir and strain into a coupette glass.

Garnish with Norfolk sorrel leaf. — James made a rich rum based martini. He named it White Noise because although it has big flavours, it's completely clear. The beautiful thing about Diplomatico Blanco, and what James wanted to convey within this martini, is its complexities and creamy malted milk richness, which comes from being produced using 100% Venezuelan sugar cane and aged two years in white oak casks. The sorrel is a citrus bomb to be eaten at the end as a palate cleanser after the creamy rich martini.

drinks.title: White Russian
drinks.history: Gustave Tops mixed the Black Russian at the Hotel Metropole in Brussels in 1949 for Perle Mesta, the American ambassador to Luxembourg. Adding cream turns it white, a version first found in print in 1965. The Big Lebowski brought it back from the dead in 1998.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice, then add vodka and coffee liqueur.
Float cream on top and stir gently just before drinking.
-- Forever associated with The Dude in The Big Lebowski, who calls it a "Caucasian".

drinks.title: Wild Nettle Cordial
drinks.author: Abigail Clephane
steps: Bring water, white sugar, and citric acid to a boil in a pot.
Add nettles washed fresh or dried and remove from the heat. Infuse for a couple of hours 120 minutes, then strain through a fine sieve.

Funnel into a sterilised bottle, store in the fridge and consume within 2 weeks, or freeze until needed. — For a longer-lasting syrup, add more sugar and bring it back to the boil for a couple of minutes before bottling and sealing.

drinks.title: Woo Woo
drinks.history: Out of the same peach schnapps boom as Sex on the Beach, minus the orange juice. No creator is recorded.
steps: Shake vodka, peach schnapps and cranberry juice hard with ice.
Strain into a glass over fresh ice.
-- A sweet, fruity 1980s staple — three ingredients, easy to remember, easier to drink.

drinks.title: Woo Woo Shot
drinks.history: The Woo Woo cut down to a shot. Peach schnapps was to the 1980s what elderflower was to the 2010s, and this is the plainest evidence of it.
steps: Shake vodka, peach schnapps and cranberry juice briefly with ice, then strain into a shot glass.

drinks.title: Yellow Belly
drinks.author: Simon Difford
steps: Add citrus vodka, limoncello, lemon juice and sugar syrup to a shaker filled with ice. Shake well and strain into a chilled glass.

drinks.title: Yellow Belly Martini
steps: Add limoncello, lemon vodka, and lemon juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
Shake well and strain into a chilled martini glass.

drinks.title: Zombie
drinks.history: Donald \"Don the Beachcomber\" Beach kept the recipe secret by pre-mixing it into numbered, unlabelled bottles his own staff could not decode. Customers were limited to two. Jeff \"Beachbum\" Berry finally reconstructed the original from a former barman's notebooks in the 2000s.
steps: Shake white rum, dark rum, overproof rum, lime juice, falernum and apricot brandy hard with ice.
Strain into a tall glass over crushed ice and float grenadine on top.
Garnish with a sprig of mint.
-- Created by "Don the Beachcomber" in 1930s Hollywood, and famously limited to two per customer.
